app.name: Shambala
app.description:
Drop the outside world at the gates and dive into four days of Adventures in Utopia…

For over 25 years, Shambala has been the UK’s fiercely independent, seriously silly, wildly creative and radically sustainable festival.

Every August Bank Holiday, we transform the stunning countryside estate of Kelmarsh Hall and Gardens near Market Harborough, Northamptonshire, into a vibrant playground of music, performance, arts, dance, wellbeing, workshops and woodland parties.

Completely independent and family-friendly, Shambala is a place to discover, explore and fuel-up on creativity!

At Shambala, you’ll find around 40 venues, covering all manner of art forms – from big musical stages, to dozens of microvenues, nooks and crannies, covering everything from techno to dancehall to folk, to disco.

We’ve got venues dedicated to poetry, puppetry, politics and permaculture to name but a few, an enchanted woodland packed with art installations and surprises, one of the best kid’s fields on the circuit, a gorgeous healing meadow with free yoga and meditation classes running all day, dance workshops, a legendary fancy dress carnival, and even our very own (shambolic) Olympic Games. sadasd

entities.name: Sukanya & Arrival Sound
entities.description:
Sukanya & Arrival Sound

Sukanya from Kolkata and Arrival sound from the uk bring positive Reggae music with deeply rooted themes of nature, divine femininity and celebration of life. They flow through lovers rock, rub-a-dub, roots and steppas. Expect deep vibrations, a sizzling live brass section, connected bass and drum, psychoacoustic effects, positive energy and dancing. 

Their collaboration began from a shared love of reggae music and the now infamous sunsplash festival in Goa. The first song together was ‘Falling Down’ featuring General Zooz, an epic about power structures and the need for systemic change, the second release was a lovers rock love story called ‘Darling Darling’, quickly followed by the ‘Timeless Connection EP’, three tracks exploring nature, divine femininity and ancestry. The latest offering is ‘Celebration song’, destined to make you dance and celebrate this existence we share. 

Together their sound, energy and vibration is in perfect harmony. Working and vibrating across continents connecting people and bringing dance floors to life wherever they play.

What started as a course for nine women to learn the art of DJing has exploded into a powerhouse of talent pushing against gender imbalance in the local scene.

Rooted in community, driven by basslines and built on sisterhood, MiXXlab represents a new wave of selectors with diverse sounds, styles and stories. entities.name: GANNA
entities.description:
Berlin-based Ukrainian artist GANNA brings a spellbinding solo performance - an immersive journey where ancient tradition meets bold contemporary sound. For over a decade, she has been reimagining the rich folklore of her homeland, transforming archival songs into vivid, modern soundscapes that resonate far beyond their origins. 

On stage, GANNA creates entire worlds in real time. Using loops, effects, samples, and the guitar synth, she builds layered compositions from a single melodic line, her voice guiding the audience through shifting textures of rhythm and harmony. What begins simply unfolds into a rich and unpredictable sonic landscape—at once deeply rooted in Ukrainian tradition and strikingly contemporary. 

Her repertoire draws on fieldwork across Ukraine, shaped by encounters with village singers and oral histories passed down through generations. These fragments of memory are reimagined with urgency and imagination, giving voice to a culture that continues to endure and evolve. 

Having performed at major international showcases including WOMEX and Reeperbahn Festival, GANNA now presents her powerful solo set - offering a performance that is as moving as it is electrifying.

entities.name: Kadialy Kouyate
entities.description:
Born into the distinguished Kouyate griot lineage of southern Senegal, Kadialy Kouyate is an
internationally acclaimed kora virtuoso, singer, composer and educator. As a descendant of one of
West Africa's most celebrated hereditary musical families, he was immersed from an early age in
the Mandinka griot tradition, a centuries-old practice of preserving history, storytelling and cultural
knowledge through music. Drawing on this rich heritage, Kadialy has developed a distinctive artistic
voice that seamlessly bridges traditional West African music and contemporary global sounds

Widely recognised as one of the leading kora players of his generation in the United Kingdom,
Kadialy has built a multifaceted career spanning international performance, recording, theatre,
broadcasting and education. He has worked with and collaborated alongside renowned
artists including Baaba Maal, Abel Selaocoe, Shabaka Hutchings, Mahalia, Pa Salieu, Greentea Peng and Sampha. 

Drawing upon generations of musical heritage preserved within his family's sound archive, Kadialy, along with his quartet, reimagine traditional West African songs through original compositions that honour the past while speaking to contemporary audiences.

entities.name: That God Damn Poetry Jam Presents
entities.description:
THIS IS THE POETRY JAM, THAT GOD DAMN POETRY JAM  

Coming from London's cultural borough of Camden, THAT GOD DAMN POETRY JAM brings the hypest night in town! A safe space where all are welcome and everyone gets a chance to speak. Hosted by Kid Anansi, THAT GOD DAMN POETRY JAM will feature guest poets Becksy Becks and Jah-Mir Early.

Kid Anansi
The poetic equivalent of finding out that the drinks machine in your local McDonalds has replaced its Pepsi button with spiced rum. Kid Anansi is confusing, frightening, delicious with ginger ale and lemon, and unhealthy in large doses. His poetry will have you laughing, crying, biting your knuckles in second-hand embarrassment, or all three, mixing history and melancholy with slapstick humour and inimitable energy. A regular face on the BAFTA Award winning first season of Life & Rhymes, and host of poetry nights around London. 

Becksy Becks
Becksy Becks is a “seemingly”" functional Poet navigating the beautiful chaos of adulthood. This Birmingham raised, South Sudanese, Poet creates vivid visual storytelling through words delivered in her signature conversational style. Her work sits on the fine line between humour and the hard truths your
therapist warned you about. To best describe Becksy Becks is to call her a Poet on Purpose, Dancer by Daydream and Awesome by Everything else.

Jah-Mir Early
He is older than he looks, improves poetry by using his dyslexia, ADHD and empathy to reach his audiences, whether with a live Band or just alone with the people. He has been an invited guest artist for the BBC Edinburgh Fringe Slam. Jah-Mir Early also debuted his all-improv poetry show #BeSpoken at the Edinburgh Fringe... and came away mostly sane.

entities.name: Organising Against Fascism
entities.description:
Organising Against Fascism: How to Unite Communities in the Face of Rising Far-Right Activity in the UK

As far-right movements continue to grow across the UK, the need for collective resistance has never been more urgent. This panel brings together organisers, activists, cultural workers, and political voices to explore how communities can respond to fascism through solidarity, political action, and grassroots organising.

Speaking from a national political perspective, Zack Polanski will reflect on the broader social and political conditions enabling the rise of the far right, and the importance of building inclusive movements capable of resisting authoritarianism while offering real alternatives rooted in justice and democracy.

Ashley Joiner of Queercircle will offer an institutional perspective, exploring how cultural and community organisations can create spaces of belonging, challenge exclusionary narratives, and support marginalised communities in times of increasing hostility and division.

Shanice McBean — feminist, Marxist activist, writer, and co-author of Abolition Revolution — will speak from a grassroots perspective, drawing on traditions of community organising, abolitionist politics, and mutual aid to examine how local networks of care and resistance can confront fascism at its roots.

The discussion will be chaired by André Jahnoi, a Liverpool-born hip-hop artist, community organiser, and decolonial thinker whose work is grounded in his Afro-Jamaican heritage and commitment to cultural resistance, liberation, and community empowerment.

Together, the panel will explore how political engagement, cultural organising, and grassroots action can work in tandem to build resilient communities capable of resisting fear, division, and authoritarianism. At its core, resisting fascism means creating a society rooted in equality, care, dignity, and collective liberation.

Eating Otherwise is a participatory exploration of food as a technology of care — blending sensory practice, collective reflection, storytelling, and shared tasting. Together, we’ll explore food not just as fuel, but as a site of memory, pleasure, politics, improvisation, and relational care.

Grounded in Black diasporic foodways, this workshop draws on ritual, collective participation, and embodied experience to explore how food shapes the ways we connect, survive, gather, and imagine different futures together.

Expect conversation, reflection, shared sensory experiences, and space to think differently about what it means to be nourished — individually and collectively.

Safiya Robinson (also known as sisterwoman) is a chef, interdisciplinary facilitator, and culinary artist exploring food as a site of memory, culture, and care. Through workshops, participatory meals, writing, and The Intentional Nourishment Podcast, she creates embodied experiences rooted in dignity, pleasure, and meaningful connection.

entities.name: Film screening: Everybody to Kenmure Street + post-screening conversation
entities.description:
In May 2021, a UK Home Office dawn raid in Glasgow sparks one of the most powerful acts of community resistance seen in recent years. In Pollokshields, Scotland’s most diverse neighbourhood, hundreds of local residents gather in the street to stop the deportation of their neighbours — bringing food, solidarity, and collective courage to a moment of fear and uncertainty.

Directed by Felipe Bustos Sierra, Everybody to Kenmure Street is a moving documentary about what happens when ordinary people refuse to look away. At once intimate and political, it captures the energy of a community standing together in real time, and asks urgent questions about borders, belonging, civil resistance, and what it means to show up for one another when it matters.

The screening will be followed by a conversation exploring some of the themes raised in the film, including solidarity, collective action, and community under pressure.

Dir: Felipe Bustos Sierra

English / 98m

entities.name: Resolve & Reflect: Mindful Conflict Management
entities.description:
Join this interactive workshop to discover practical strategies for managing conflict and creating healthier, more constructive interactions in any setting. You’ll learn the fundamentals of conflict management, including how to identify the root causes of disagreements, recognise patterns that escalate tension, and navigate challenging situations with confidence and clarity.

We’ll also introduce the basics of Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), a helpful approach to responding to conflict mindfully. Through ACT techniques, you’ll learn how to reduce the emotional impact of disagreements, accept situations beyond your control, and focus on actions aligned with your values. These practices help you manage both internal stress and external tensions more effectively, leaving you better equipped to handle conflict calmly and intentionally.

A core part of the workshop focuses on personal boundaries—an essential tool for maintaining healthy relationships and reducing unnecessary difficulties. You’ll explore strategies to set clear, respectful boundaries, communicate your needs assertively, and protect your emotional well-being.

By combining conflict management skills, ACT principles, and boundary-setting techniques, this workshop offers a holistic approach to resolving disagreements, fostering resilience, and enhancing interpersonal effectiveness. You’ll leave with practical tools to reduce conflict, strengthen your relationships, and navigate challenges with greater ease and confidence.

Stress affects all of us differently. Sometimes we become anxious, overwhelmed or reactive. Other times we shut down, disconnect, or struggle to cope at all. This workshop explores the idea of the Window of Tolerance — a simple but powerful framework for understanding how our nervous systems respond under pressure.

Together we’ll explore how to recognise when you’re feeling grounded and present, versus when stress or overwhelm pushes you beyond your capacity. Through gentle, practical exercises, you’ll learn ways to regulate your nervous system, respond rather than react, and build a kinder relationship with yourself when things feel difficult.

The session will include grounding practices, mindfulness, self-compassion tools, and reflection on personal triggers, limits, and patterns. Rather than trying to “fix” yourself, this workshop invites a deeper understanding of how your system works — and what helps you feel safer, steadier, and more connected to yourself.

A calm, interactive and supportive space. No previous experience needed.

entities.name: Sam Redmore
entities.description:
A hugely respected DJ in his hometown of Birmingham and long-standing resident at seminal club nights including Leftfoot and Magic Door, Sam Redmore has built a formidable reputation as one of the UK’s most exciting and versatile selectors and producers.

He truly broke onto the UK music scene in 2022 with the release of his debut album “Universal Vibrations” - a vibrant, wide-ranging collection of global grooves and eclectic dancefloor heaters capable of igniting any party. The record was met with widespread acclaim and strong radio backing. BBC Radio 6 Music championed the album - spinning standout single “Nagu” over 100 times - and invited Sam to contribute guest mixes for key tastemakers such as Craig Charles, Huey Morgan, Afrodeutsche and Cerys Matthews. Further support followed from BBC Radio 1, NTS Radio, Rinse FM, Worldwide FM and Jazz FM - where the album was awarded Album of the Week - alongside international plays on KCRW, FIP and 2SER.

Redmore built on that momentum in October 2025 with the release of his second album “Modulate” - a dancefloor-focused record that blends electronic and programmed elements with rich live instrumentation. Modulate further cemented Sam’s reputation for crafting forward-thinking, globally influenced dance music. The album features collaborations with internationally esteemed artists including Dele Sosimi and Abdominal, as well as the track “Pride,” originally commissioned as the theme music for Joe Lycett’s stand-up show.

Sam is currently working on a guest mix for Gilles Peterson’s show on BBC Radio 6 Music - a natural fit given Peterson’s long-standing championing of global and eclectic sounds. Beyond radio, Sam has cultivated a huge and highly engaged online following, regularly sharing selections and insights that showcase both his DJ skills and his deep-rooted love and knowledge of music - spanning funk, disco, house and broken beat through to afrobeat, cumbia, salsa and samba.

These wide-ranging influences are central to Sam’s identity as both producer and DJ. Whether delivering an all-night-long journey that transcends genres or a tightly focused set packed with the choicest disco, house and broken beat cuts, Redmore has the taste, technical skill and musical intuition to move any dancefloor.

With his 2026 diary already filling fast, Sam Redmore continues to cement his status as one of the UK’s most in-demand DJs - a selector and producer whose passion, versatility and global perspective truly set him apart.

entities.name: Samatha Meditation with Vijay Khuttan
entities.description:
Samatha means calm concentration and is an important stage for all forms of meditation. The technique requires a focus on the breathing in order to quiet down the mind and bring it to a state of rest or peace which is very blissful. 

The more the mind is able not to be caught up in restless thoughts the more energy it conserves and this can build up to a significant level to a point where there is a state of absorption which the ancients called “Jhana” and it is these states that the human mind aspires to in terms of spiritual development.

Without knowledge of Jhana it is difficult to progress on the path and Samatha forms of meditation are crucial to its attainment. Any meditation that works towards Jhana can be called Samatha meditation but the technique which we teach comes from Thailand. The person who brought the tradition to the UK is a person by the name of Nai Boonman and he is considered the founder of Samatha Meditation.

The technique as taught by Nai Boonman involves 16 stages and depending on your temperament progress can be swift or hard fought.

entities.name: Movement Meditatiion with Stephen Mulley
entities.description:
In these Movement meditation sessions we will be using gentle body movements, breathwork, and active physical positions to help us find a sense of peace, calm, and relaxation. 

We will focus more on the movements of the body rather than the goal of any movement. 

As with all meditation, the key is to be present in the moment, and, by giving our full attention to our body and movements, we can find another route into mindfulness. 

Stephen will lead you in noticing your muscles and joints as they move, or the feeling of your feet against the ground or the air against your skin. We’ll pay attention to the body and how it feels as it moves, bends, and twists. Even your breathing, heartbeat, and other inner sensations can be better noticed through movement and when you are mindful of the body. Movement meditation can be particularly good if you aren’t in the mood for sitting still!

The movements themselves will be simple and accessible for everyone.

Workshops will include needle-felted ears, alongside sauna hats, flower headpieces, and a relaxed drop-in free-flow session where participants can contribute to a collaborative felted mural created across the weekend.

entities.name: Feeding the Future Through Agroecology
entities.description:
What does it mean to build a food system rooted in solidarity, ecology, and collective care rather than extraction and profit?

Join Jyoti Fernandes — smallholder farmer, co-founder of the Land Workers’ Alliance, and spokesperson for the global peasant movement La Via Campesina — for a powerful conversation on the growing agroecology movement in the UK and beyond.

Drawing on decades of organising, farming, and political advocacy, Jyoti will explore how small-scale farmers and grassroots movements are resisting industrial agriculture while actively building alternatives: from local food systems and cooperative models to agroforestry, climate resilience, and land justice.

This talk will look at how communities are coming together to defend biodiversity, livelihoods, and food sovereignty in the face of ecological breakdown — and why diverse grassroots voices must be at the centre of shaping the future of farming.

entities.name: Exploring the Un-Big
entities.description:
Calling all geeks! In a festival of 15,000 people, there must be some, and you might enjoy sessions like this, where nothing much happens except you get to examine weird little plants (and some creepy-crawlies) using illuminated lenses and digital microscopes.

The lead characters are two different kinds of ‘primitive’ plants, mosses and lichens, that both have huge pedigrees going back hundreds of millions of years, found all over the world in all seasons with thousands of different kinds. Each has a claim to be The Plants What Conquered The Land, creating stuff to eat for the animals, who came ashore later. Plants roll their own food from the sun, cunning blighters. 

Anyway, it can be enlightening to find that what you thought was a just a green fuzz in the pavement, or a chewing-gum stain, is actually a distinguished organism with a complicated sex-life, possibly like yourself.

Join a botanical arch-geek in the woods and fields surrounding the festival site, in search of the descendants of those early pioneers, without which you might not be here at all.

entities.name: Food from the Wild: Growing Within Rewilded Landscapes
entities.description:
Can rewilding and food production work together?

This workshop explores practical ways to combine wild food harvesting with rewilding projects, wildlife gardens, and biodiverse growing spaces. Drawing on hands-on experience from projects in Yorkshire, we’ll look at how humans can work alongside natural systems to create landscapes that support both ecological restoration and sustainable food production.

We’ll cover approaches to incorporating edible and medicinal plants into rewilded environments, encouraging biodiversity while also creating resilient sources of food and forage.

Topics may include:

Designing spaces that balance wildness and productivity
Useful edible and medicinal species for rewilding projects
Encouraging biodiversity through planting choices
Working with natural systems rather than controlling them
Wild harvesting approaches and considerations

This session is ideal for growers, gardeners, foragers, and anyone interested in creating richer relationships between people, food, and the living landscapes around them.

A tasting workshop exploring migration, food appropriation, diaspora, and notions of home through shared flavours, stories, conversation, and collective reflection.

Emerging from anthropological research into food and politics in the SWANA region and diasporic communities in the UK, Blessed Hands invites participants to reflect on questions of authenticity, memory, movement, and cultural inheritance through the act of tasting together.

Led by Dr Michal Nahman and joined by artist, facilitator, and composer Aisha Ali, the session will include a short introduction, food tasting, discussion, and shared exploration of how food carries histories of migration, displacement, survival, and belonging.

Tastings may include dishes such as bean stew, rose jam, bread, olive oil, and za’atar.

Michal’s research traces her own family heritage from the Spanish expulsion of Jews and Muslims through Italy, Greece, and Turkey, and connects to her wider work with the Land Stories Collective in Bristol, supporting food and land education, justice, and solidarity with Palestine and South Lebanon.

Aisha brings experience working across performance, music, activism, and community food projects, including Speak & Eat — a cookery and ESOL programme supporting refugees and asylum seekers through shared food and language.

entities.name: Planting Wishes for the Future

What kind of future do we want to grow together?

In this collaborative art workshop, festival-goers are invited to help create a living Garden of Wishes using recycled and reclaimed materials. Together we’ll make dandelions, seed heads, and plant forms carrying hopes, intentions, and visions for a fairer, more regenerative future.

Inspired by seed dispersal, resilience, and collective care, the installation will continue growing across the festival as more people add their own wishes and reflections.

Participants can create their own contribution, read messages left by others, or simply spend time in a gentle creative space shaped by imagination, hope, and shared humanity.

Alongside the installation will be links to further resources exploring community-led climate action and the idea of a just transition — connecting personal reflection with wider social change.

Join us for:
• a grounded, people-centred understanding of just transition
• insight into how community-led action can influence policy change
• a sense of agency, connection, and belonging
• the experience of contributing to a shared, hopeful, living artwork

entities.name: Stone Soup: Cooking Up Community Together
entities.description:
Inspired by the traditional folk story Stone Soup, this communal kitchen gathering asks what becomes possible when everybody brings something small to the table.

Led by Carrie Vallance, founder of Food Troops CIC in Redruth, Cornwall, the session will slowly build a shared pot of soup from surplus and rescued vegetables — weaving together practical food skills with conversation around community, care, resilience, and mutual support.

Drawing on seven years of running a community kitchen and garden project, Carrie will share how Food Troops rescues surplus produce from farms and supermarkets and transforms it into nourishing meals, preserves, ferments, connection, and local resilience.

As the pot simmers, so will the conversation: how do we turn waste into care? What helps people feel safe, fed, connected, and supported? What kinds of communities do we want to build when times are hard?

This is part demo, part gathering, part shared meal. At the end, the soup will be served ahead of the screening of Everybody to Kenmure Street — so the audience can walk into a film about solidarity, resistance, and collective action having already shared food together.

entities.name: Is it Cultural Appropriation? with Sheila Menon
entities.description:
Most of us have heard of cultural appropriation but many aren’t sure what it really means, or what counts as cultural appropriation and what doesn’t. Often, the starting point of any conversation about the subject is this question: “Is it cultural appropriation?!” Or maybe we even hear the question: “Is it cultural appreciation or cultural appropriation?” 
 
But both of these questions lead to a very binary (black & white) way of understanding what is actually an extremely nuanced and contextual conversation. 
 
In this talk/workshop Sheila aims to help unpick and explore these nuances and contexts in which this conversation sits, to help better understand the implications of certain choices we might make, so that we can apply this understanding to our everyday lives. 
 
Sheila is a trainer/facilitator working broadly around themes related to all forms of systemic oppression, to help better understand them - how they work, how they impact us, and how we reproduce them.

entities.name: On Homecoming: Finding Your Place & Contribution in Uncertain Times
entities.description:
What does it mean to find your place and contribution in a time when so many old systems, identities, and ideas of success no longer seem to make sense?

In this thoughtful and deeply personal talk, Ramona Fricke explores why so many people — especially those drawn to changemaking, healing, creativity, or community work — are struggling to find orientation right now. As we come into closer contact with the limitations and contradictions within our political, social, ecological, and personal systems, it can become difficult to know where we fit, what we truly believe in, or how to move forward.

Drawing on personal story, a decade of Social Impact work across organisational forms, world regions and cause areas, and years of supporting others through her coaching practice, Ramona explores how we might build a different kind of inner navigation system: one rooted not in performance or certainty, but in relationship, place, seasonality, regenerative principles and deep self-attunement.

This is a talk for anyone questioning their path, navigating transition, or searching for a more grounded and authentic way to contribute in complex times.

entities.name: Witchcraft, Altered States and the Feminist Anarchism of Native Power Plants
entities.description:
Broomsticks, wanking, beer brewing, flying and herbalism - what do they all have in common?  Come and explore in this workshop run by the Seed Sistas.

Learn about the historical perspective of the flying witch, how she flew, where to and what with… it’s not just a load of old wank but some of it is.  

As medical herbalists and practitioners of magic we Seed Sistas have been working with the witching herbs, the nightshades for decades.  While others seek mind-bending plants from forests thousands of miles away, in the back garden of the European Witch grows some of the most powerful medicinal and magical herbs known to woman. 

Dip your toe into the green unguent, a healing formula concocted to connect you with the wilds. Learn of its history and current applications, the legalities and more as we go on a journey into the witches’ spellbook and come flying into the modern era with healing medicine for all. 

Adults only

entities.name: The Great Mandrake Robbery: A Talk by the Seed Sistas
entities.description:
Step right up for a wildly entertaining herbal caper with the Seed Sistas — Fi and Kaz — herbalists, witches, plant nerds and botanical mischief-makers on a mission to rescue one of the world’s most notorious herbs from myth, fear and modern-day censorship.

In The Great Mandrake Robbery, the Seed Sistas unearth the twisted tale of Mandrake, the legendary screaming root once prized for magic, medicine, fertility and ritual, before it was buried beneath folklore, fearmongering and legislation. Through theatre, storytelling, herbal history and plenty of irreverent sass, they journey from ancient tombs and witch trials to Shakespeare, flying ointments and the unfortunate “screaming baby plant” made famous by Hollywood.

But this isn’t just a history lesson. It’s a plant-powered rebellion. Discover how Mandrake became feared, forbidden and misunderstood, and why reclaiming our relationship with powerful plants matters more than ever. Expect laughter, myth-busting, botanical weirdness and deliciously dark tales from the herbal underground.

Medicine. Magic. Mischief.

Mandrake is rising again… are you ready to hear it scream?

entities.name: What If You’re Not Broken? Healing, Neurodivergence and Coming Home to Yourself
entities.description:
You’ve tried the healing modalities. The retreats, therapy, yoga, breathwork, nervous system work, maybe even plant medicine. Some of it helped. Some of it felt transformative. But somehow, nothing quite seems to stick.

Maybe you’ve spent years wondering why life feels harder for you than it seems to for other people. Maybe you keep searching for the next thing that might finally help you become who you’re supposed to be.

This workshop is for people who are neurodivergent — or beginning to suspect they might be — and wondering whether part of what they’ve been trying to “heal” is actually the way they’re wired.

Together, we’ll explore what becomes possible when you stop trying to force yourself into someone else’s version of normal and begin relating to yourself with more honesty, understanding, and acceptance.

This is a gentle, grounded and interactive session with invitations to reflect throughout. There’s no pressure to share, perform, or participate in any particular way. You’re welcome exactly as you are.

entities.description:
The self-improvement world often sells us the idea that we are unfinished projects — that if we do enough healing, enough courses, enough work on ourselves, we’ll eventually arrive at the version of us that finally feels whole.

Many of us have spent years inside that loop.

This workshop is for anyone beginning to question whether the constant search for transformation has quietly become exhausting. What happens when healing becomes another form of striving? What happens when you stop chasing the next breakthrough and start listening to what’s already here?

Together we’ll explore the pressure to optimise, evolve and endlessly “work on ourselves,” and what it might mean to step outside that cycle — even briefly — and meet ourselves with a little more compassion.

Expect honest reflection, gentle interaction, and a space that values slowness over performance. There’s no expectation to share anything you don’t want to. Come as you are.

entities.name: Why Are There Goats at Shambala?
entities.description:
Why are there goats at Shambala — and what can they teach us about food, farming, land, and care?

In this practical and thought-provoking session, Patrick shares the story of Street Goat, a Bristol-based community food project he co-founded in 2015. Street Goat brings people together to collectively manage and care for livestock in urban areas, producing milk and meat while reconnecting people with the realities of food and farming.

We’ll explore how the project turned unused urban land into a working goat dairy and grazing project, how the collective model works in practice, and what it means for ordinary people to become part-time farmers in the city.

From shared milking shifts and affordable local milk to grazing overgrown allotments and bringing land back into food production, Street Goat opens up bigger questions about food sovereignty, animal agriculture, sustainability, and our relationship with the animals we eat from — or care for.

entities.name: From Forest to Furniture: Why Provenance Matters
entities.description:
Think about a piece of wooden furniture you own. Who made it? And most importantly—where did the timber come from?

Wood is an extraordinary, versatile material, yet it is becoming increasingly scarce. With global deforestation progressing at an alarming rate, Britain bears a significant share of responsibility for how we source our timber. If we don’t change our relationship with this resource, we risk losing the very landscapes that provide it.

Despite the stakes, there is a way to turn the demand for quality wood into a force for restoration. By focusing on British species—such as the characterful grain of English Oak, the resilience of Ash, or the warmth of Sweet Chestnut—we can create a cycle that supports active woodland management.

Sating our appetite for beautiful products doesn't have to come at the cost of the environment. In fact, through conscious craftsmanship, it can help fund the future of our forests.

Join Alex for a relaxed talk exploring how we can harvest wood and reforest the planet at the same time. He'll discuss why the provenance of our timber is a vital tool for conservation and how making furniture responsibly can be a deliberate step towards a more sustainable British landscape.

Through somatic practices, Yoga, breath exploration, mindful inquiry and experiential meditation, you’ll be invited to honour your body as a sacred space and a place of belonging in this life. These resources support you in attuning to the quieter layers of your inner landscape and in recognising the body’s innate intelligence.
Restoring the nervous system is a process that requires radical authenticity, honest listening and discernment. These qualities help us meet ourselves with care, connect with community more fully, and soften more deeply into relationship with the earth.

Designed as a collective moment of recalibration within the wider pulse of Shambala, Somanaut supports you to anchor into a felt sense of inner wholeness.
This is an invitation to land back home in the body - resilient, present and safe.

No previous experience needed, only a willingness to explore.

entities.name: Deaf Poetry Showcase ft Ishtiaq Hussain & Zoë McWhinney
entities.description:
For over 15 years, Ishtiaq Hussain has been captivating audiences with his exceptional skill in Visual Vernacular (VV) a dynamic performance style that combines facial expressions, mime, body movement, and iconic gestures to tell powerful, visually engaging stories. His work goes beyond spoken language, creating theatre that is accessible, emotional, and deeply resonant for people of all ages and backgrounds.

Offstage, Ishtiaq is passionate about sharing his VV expertise and knowledge. He supports artists and creatives in incorporating VV and British Sign Language (BSL) into their own work, offering training and mentorship to promote inclusion through visual storytelling.

Zoë McWhinney introduces poetry that is bold, fearless and vital. Expect work that combines lyric intensity with clarity, humour and urgency. No prior poetry knowledge required, just curiosity. A rare chance to encounter some of the most exciting writing today. Curated by the Forward Prizes for Poetry, this special reading brings outstanding contemporary poetry to the heart of Shambala. 

Zoë McWhinney is a BSL poet and Visual Vernacular performer based in South East London. She has performed at renowned venues such as The Roundhouse and the United Nations in Geneva and made history as the first Deaf poet published in British Sign Language in Modern Poetry in Translation magazine. Her recent work includes adapting Ilya Kaminsky’s Deaf Republic for The Royal Court Theatre, in partnership with Dead Centre theatre company. In addition to her writing, Zoë works as an actor and director.

entities.name: Antisemitism and Anti-Racist Movements
entities.description:
What is structural antisemitism - its history, contours, and manifestations today? And what is its relationship to Islamophobia, anti-Black and colonial racisms? In this talk Shanice will bring to light the too often forgotten connections between Jews and other racialised groups. As well as exploring the ruptures; from Jewish ethno-nationalism, to the West's reinvention of itself as the protector of Jews. Concluding with some provocations on what this means for left and anti-racist movements today, Shanice will invite the audience to share their thoughts. 

Shanice McBean is a feminist and Marxist activist and writer. She is the co-author of Abolition Revolution, 2023 winner of the Bread and Roses Award for Radical Publishing. She is also co-host of the Life of the Party podcast. Shanice grew up in Handsworth, Birmingham, before settling down in Tottenham, London.

entities.name: Fork This Mess: How Food Choices Can Change the World
entities.description:
Food sits at the heart of some of the biggest challenges we face — from climate change and pollution to public health, food insecurity, and social inequality. But can changing what we eat really make a difference?

Join Patrick from PETA for an engaging and accessible conversation exploring how plant-based choices can positively impact humans, other animals, and the planet. Together we’ll unpack the hidden costs of industrial animal farming, including its links to zoonotic diseases, antibiotic resistance, environmental damage, and the disproportionate impact these systems can have on marginalised communities.

Alongside the bigger picture, this session also offers practical, grounded guidance for anyone curious about eating more plant-based — whether through small everyday swaps or a fully vegan lifestyle. Expect useful tips, honest discussion, and space for questions, all rooted in Shambala values of kindness, fairness, and collective care.

entities.name: Changing the World Without Leaving People Behind
entities.description:
Climate action doesn’t happen in isolation from the rest of life. Housing, food, transport, energy, health, poverty, and inequality are all deeply connected — and any meaningful response to the climate crisis has to begin there.

This participatory talk explores what community-led climate action can look like in real life, especially in areas facing deprivation and systemic inequality. Drawing on lived experience and grassroots organising, we’ll explore how trust-building, local leadership, and collective action can create change that is not only sustainable, but fair.

Together we’ll reflect on:

Why climate justice and social justice cannot be separated
What happens when communities shape solutions for themselves
How ordinary people can influence systems and power structures
What it means to create change that people can actually participate in

This is a conversational and reflective session rather than a lecture — a space for honest discussion about how we move towards futures that care for both people and planet.

entities.name: Gaumarjos! The Art of Toasting with Anna Rose Hope
entities.description:
Anna invites you on a magical journey into the supranatural… an exploratory space where we will use the ancient Georgian art of toasting as a way of deepening our understanding of ourselves and our connection to the world around us. 

In this fun and experiential workshop, we will explore the Georgian tradition of Supra - ritualised toasting - as a way of getting more intimate with the depth and breadth of our own experience. 

As Tamada, or toastmaster, Anna will lead participants through an embodied, playful practice of observation and appreciation, building our confidence to find and express our own unique voice in the supportive company of others. 

Together we’ll explore authentic ways to connect with our hearts, bodies, emotions, minds and intuition, and to share our appreciation with others, co-creating community one toast at a time. Gaumarjos! 

Dr Anna Rose Hope is on a journey to explore what it means to be more authentically human. As a ‘doctor of community’, her work spans from academia to hands-on, playful workshops and rituals. Weaving together the five elements of Tibetan Buddhism and the Georgian feasting and toasting tradition of ‘supra’, she is discovering and sharing more embodied ways of experiencing the world around us. These experiences enable us to build connection and community with greater awareness, intention and honesty.

entities.name: Creating a Conscious Planet
entities.description:
What if the most crucial act we can take is to become more conscious? 

In this interactive session, volunteers from Conscious Planet explore how inner wellbeing and outer action are two sides of the same coin. When people become more aware, more joyful, and more clear within themselves, responsible action towards the planet and each other naturally follows. 

Through a short video from yogi and visionary Sadhguru, an engaging discussion, and a powerful 7-minute meditation (Miracle of Mind), you'll leave equipped to revitalise your own inner wellbeing, help create a more joyful humanity, and a more conscious planet. 

This is an invitation to be part of something joyful, solution-oriented, and already spanning continents.

Over the course of three decades, Conscious Planet’s path-breaking environmental and social initiatives have garnered global recognition from esteemed organizations, including the United Nation and the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN), and serve as thriving models for human empowerment and community revitalization worldwide.

Eddie Reynolds - Eddie works in communications for Conscious Planet, and previously wrote children’s books about our planet, climate and natural world. He believes the health of the ground beneath our feet matters more than most of us realise, and loves finding new ways to say so.

Henry Asplin - Media Coordinator (UK/EU) for Conscious Planet, Henry works at the intersection of storytelling and the natural world, helping journalists shine a light on ecosystem restoration and inner wellbeing. #SaveSoil

entities.name: Mark Grist: Monster Rap Battle Workshop
entities.description:
Mark Grist is a multi-award-winning poet, rap battler, children’s author and former teacher whose performances and videos have been viewed more than 100 million times online. A pioneer in bringing poetry to new audiences through battle rap, storytelling and live performance, he has appeared on the BBC, Channel 4 and Red Bull, and has twice been honoured at the International Webby Awards. 

Mark's previous titles include Poet Laureate of Peterborough, Edinburgh Fringe Slam Champion and Chief Bard of the Fens.

Mark starred in Red Bull TV’s Mark Grist Battles the World, appeared in Channel 4’s Mr Drew’s School for Boys, and is the author of acclaimed children’s books including Rhinos Don’t Cry, featured on CBeebies Bedtime Stories and read by Danny Dyer.

Mark tours schools, theatres and festivals across the world, and hosts the podcast We, The Poets — an Arts Council England-funded series exploring the craft, chaos and reality of life as a poet in the UK today.

This year marks Mark’s ninth year at Shambala Festival, where he returns to unleash the
legendary Monster Rap Battle workshop.

Workshop capacity is limited, visit The Library when you arrive on site to sign up!

entities.description:
Curated by the Forward Prizes for Poetry, this special reading brings outstanding contemporary poetry to the heart of Shambala. Showcasing  Michael Mullen, this event offers an introduction to poetry that is bold, fearless and vital. Expect work that combines lyric intensity with clarity, humour and urgency. No prior poetry knowledge required, just curiosity. A rare chance to encounter some of the most exciting writing today.

Michael Mullen is a queer poet, writer and spoken word artist from Glasgow. Writing in both Scots and Standard English, Mullen’s primary concern is Scotland – its languages and its people. Years of work in hospitality and later as a support worker has put ordinary people at the forefront of their poetry. He was the co-winner of the Edwin Morgan Poetry Award 2023-4 as well as the Scottish National Slam runner up in 2022. He appeared on Life and Rhymes with Benjamin Zephaniah on Sky Arts and his work has been published in various places including Neu! Reekie! #NeuVoices, Bella Caledonia, Paisley Mill Magazine, Rymour Books, Glasgow City of Poets and Seahorse Publications. Goonie is Michael’s first collection.

entities.name: Bradley Taylor & Friends
entities.description:
Bradley Taylor is an award-winning poet born and based in Birmingham. In 2024 he won the Roundhouse Poetry Slam, with that night marking the biggest poetry slam in history to date. In 2025 he released his debut collection ‘You Missed The Best Part’ before embarking on a nationwide tour. Bradley is also the host and curator of Piece of Work, Birmingham's premiere poetry night held at the Birmingham Museum & Art Gallery. 
 
Bradley’s work has appeared in Gutter Magazine, Shooter and Strix. More recently, he was commissioned to write a poem for Steven Knight (Peaky Blinders creators). In 2025, his performance at the Roundhouse was nominated for the Sky Arts award for poetry.  

He writes for, and about, people. 

Poets M. L. Walsh and Ray join Bradley on stage.  

M. L. Walsh is a Birmingham-based performance poet specialising in comic absurdism and the construction of narrative through voice and characterisation. Since graduating from the University of Birmingham with an MA in Creative Writing, Walsh has headlined numerous venues inside and outside of the city including the Birmingham Glee Club. Her use of the prose poetic monologue experiments with the translation of performance poetry from page to stage, and how theatrical technique (and its removal) can modify a text. 

Ray Vincent-Mills is a poet, performer, (paper)maker and facilitator based in Birmingham. 
BLACK, trans, queer & grateful Ray writes out of compulsion and opportunity to reframe their experiences in abstract ways.

entities.name: Sweat The System
entities.description:
Sweat the System is a ritual. For centuries, cultures around the world have used collective movement and music to build resilience, joy, and righteous rage - this workshop carries that legacy into a festival setting.

Being alive right now can be heavy. If you’re organising for change or navigating daily oppression, your body holds more than most people can see.

Dance and music have always been sites of resistance - places to gather, belong, feel, and transform - yet many of us have lost touch with these practices.

This workshop invites us to move what we’re carrying together, using music to reconnect with movement as resistance, connection, and collective force. Held by a collective of DJs, activists, dancers, and community organisers, we’ll move through grief and rage into joy, catharsis, and unapologetic liberation.

Session led by Rhiannon Colvin (RhiPlay), Sandhya Dave, & Somin Griffin-Dave (Somatic).

As a legendary keyboardist, singer, and songwriter, he began his career with Fela Kuti's famous Egypt 80 band before later leading the Positive Force band alongside Femi Kuti. Today, Sosimi stands as the ultimate guardian of the authentic Afrobeat sound, perfectly blending traditional African rhythms and jazz horns with heavy, hypnotic funk groove basslines. His live performances are famous worldwide for their explosive, nonstop energy, delivering complex polyrhythms that naturally force the crowd to dance. Having spent decades performing on major global festival stages, he acts as a vital musical bridge between Lagos and London. His high-octane sets deliver both a conscious party and a deep cultural education, packed with virtuosic keyboard solos, and infectious call-and-response vocals. He commands the stage with an unmatched, magnetic, and joyful charisma that captivates audiences instantly. Do not miss this  chance to see true musical royalty perform live on our stage. He brings the unstoppable spirit of Afrobeat straight to the festival, promising an unforgettable, deeply soulful experience. Prepare to move from the very first beat to the absolute last.

entities.description:
Stormy J is a Bristol-based DJ and broadcaster known for her era-fusing, time-warping sets. Her sound is shaped by her Caribbean heritage and a family legacy rooted in carnival culture, combined with the raw energy of British underground dance music. Growing up in Southend, Stormy J first cut her teeth on local dance stations in Essex before making her mark on the London airwaves. 

Now, she’s pioneering a bold new sound: jab house—a high-octane sub-genre of electronic dance music which is characterised by the fusion of jab jab culture, rave culture, house music and gutter soca music. With its driving 160 BPM tempo, four-on-the-floor beat, conch shells, horns, biscuit tins, and a spirit of extreme freedom, jab-house is designed to move bodies and liberate minds. 

Stormy J, Jonesy Wales and Atki2 join forces on Friday night for a special three hour takeover of the yard booth, expect a blistering selection of soca, jab house, amapiano, and more.

entities.name: SmokeLife Sound System
entities.description:
This year, Back a Yard is powerered by SmokeLife Sound System!

SmokeLife crew started out as Sunday sessions at the Attic & producing bedroom dubstep as a collective of friends.

They cut their teeth promoting at the Tube & Croft, putting rising names like Jazzsteppa,
Clouds, Elemental and on the same bill as Bristol heavyweights Phaelah, Thinking, Octopussy, Kidkut and Forsaken. 

After a run of free parties on a makeshift rig, then a forced move into a warehouse (after one too many noise complaints chased them out of normal housing) the crew picked up their first real bass bins, a set of RCF's once belonging to Armada/Retox. The rest of the rig soon came together along with a studio, and so did jungle and DnB alongside the dubstep, as the system kept growing. 

SmokeLife went on to run Dub Club's room 2 for years at the Black Swan, alongside AFM and DNAudio at Lakota, while linking up with Brisfest to run the garden at Stokes Croft Street Fest and the Lakota stage at Rave on Avon, plus festival slots
with Bling Bar and Wellfairies. 

Our sound system has been dormant for around 10 years while the crew pursued exciting new ventures and Golgot became a dad and put his focus on raising 2 kids and preparing for the future… but the time has come, they're back.

For Back A Yard, Suma will present a vinyl-led journey alongside DJ/MC Lilophilia, an Afro-Latina queer artist whose voice and presence bring raw dancehall energy and diasporic pride to the dancefloor.

entities.name: Gabby Gunn
entities.description:
GABBY GUNN is a London based DJ and producer whose sound sits at the intersection of acid, breaks and techno. 

Driven by a lifelong obsession with sound and live instrumentation, she brings a craft-first approach built for club culture — not algorithms — her skills on and off the decks speak for themselves.

Behind the decks or in the studio, Gabby treats DJing and production as two sides of the same discipline. Her sets are built with intent: weighty low-end, tight control of tension and release, and carefully timed shifts from aggression into moments of euphoria — always working with the crowd to shape the room and the raver experience.

Her productions follow the same principles, engineered for real systems and real spaces, with breaks and percussion that feel alive and constantly in motion. With years committed to honing her craft, she understands the rules but more importantly has the confidence to break them.

Comfortable in intimate clubs and on large festival stages (such as Glastonbury, Boomtown, Secret Garden Party and Snowboxx) her sets are defined by an instinctive ability to read and move a dancefloor.

With her debut release on Scuffed Recordings and forthcoming on NRG CRU, GABBY GUNN represents a new wave of electronic artists who lets the work speak first: focused, uncompromising, and deeply connected to the energy in the room.

Her artistry has earned industry support from Arts Council England through a Developing Your Creative Practice (DYCP) award, to being showcased by Pioneer at Amsterdam Dance Event and IMS Ibiza, as well as being selected for BBC Introducing at Creamfields. Her music has already been featured in Boiler Room sets, with a host of support from DJs including Jaguar, Chloe Robinson, Jamz Supernova, Manami and Human Movement alongside airplay across BBC Radio 1 Dance shows, Rinse FM and SWU FM.

entities.name: Akolá Tambó
entities.description:
Akolá Tambó is a pioneering traditional bullerengue music and dance group, recognised as the first of its kind outside the Americas. Founded in the UK, Akolá Tambó celebrates the ancestral rhythms and songs of Afro-Colombian bullerengue, a genre rooted in the coastal communities of Colombia’s Caribbean region.

The group’s mission is to promote bullerengue in the UK and Europe, increasing its visibility and appreciation. Through performances and educational programmes, Akolá Tambó shares the joy, healing, and cultural significance of this tradition while amplifying the voices of maestras and maestros from Colombia’s Caribbean coast. By building a community around bullerengue, they empower participants to connect with their cultural roots and express themselves collectively.

entities.name: Daisy Moon
entities.description:
Proving futurism can also be fun, Daisy Moon strikes out into the frontier of club music with an even split of head-twisting sonics and heart-rending charm.

​Make no mistake, her tracks bang with the floor miles to show for it, but the Bristol-based DJ and producer is versed in many different dimensions of electronic expression. In her hands, the emotional weight of forthright melodies and sampled voices refract through kaleidoscopic production and needlepoint sound design.
​
As a producer, Daisy has demonstrated her range from the most upfront party flair to exquisite experimentalism. Her EP on Shanti Celeste and Gramrcy’s Peach Discs, System Creak, was bursting with peak time energy shot through with a maverick glint, while her melancholic broken beat excursion ‘Reflections On A Flower Garden’ was picked for the Curl Compilation 2 curated by Mica Levi, Coby Sey and Brother May.
​
The scope of Daisy’s musicality extends to her DJ sets, which reliably lean on uptempo energy while ducking and diving into hidden pockets of dance music culture. Her scores of mixes for platforms like Crack, Fact, Daisychain or Untitled 909 are matched by her appearances at Fabric, Tresor, The White Hotel, Love International and Dimensions as outlets for the tweaked, playful club gear she holds dear.

​There’s a gleefully disruptive spirit in Daisy’s selections which extends to Off Kilter, her mix and event series. The ever-evolving concept is a showcase for under-represented artists probing at the fringes, in and outside the dance music sphere. That leaves the possibilities comfortably open for where Daisy takes the project next, indulging her curiosity and following her instinct for infectious energy.

entities.name: The Power of Loud: Fighting Fascism with Bass
entities.description:
Sound system culture has been used for generations, and continues to be used as a tool for political resistance against white supremacist capitalism. Join Critical youth sound system for an insight into this long and rich history, and learn how to build your own sound system. Fresh from building a soundsystem with a youth group in Oxford they will share their experiences, discuss the practical challenges and how they overcame them, as well highlighting their vision for the future as a sound system fighting against political oppression. This will be followed by a Q&A.

Critical youth sound system is a QTBPOC politically-charged sound system, birthed from the student protest scene in Newcastle and finding a home in the streets and squats of London, with connections to the squatting movement. Our work focuses on breaking down the barriers to accessing soundsystem culture for young people, QTBPOC and disabled people.

The session will be held by: 
- Maxine (DJ and organiser) 
- Amo (queer Iranian organiser) 
- Jeni (DJ, organiser, member of QTBPOC rave and protest soundsystems Critical Youth Sound and L.A.D.S and researcher into transformative justice in the music industry)

entities.name: POP-UP: Corn Dolly Workshops
entities.description:
Join Vic's pop-up corn dolly workshops, offering a lively and accessible introduction to this traditional craft. These drop-in sessions are designed for high participation events, with space for around eight people at a time. Each small corn dolly  a traditional style known as a harvest knot takes approximately 15–20 minutes to complete, allowing for up to 25–30 participants per hour.

Using a simple and highly accessible plaiting technique, suitable for most abilities, participants will quickly learn the basics of corn dolly making while creating their own piece to take home. Along the way, we’ll explore the history, folklore, and mythology of this ancient craft, as well as the cultural significance of harvest traditions.

The workshop also introduces the qualities of heritage straw, including how it is grown, sourced, and the challenges involved in keeping this traditional material alive. A fast-paced, engaging, and informative craft experience, perfect for curious drop-in participants of all ages.

Times change daily so please just pop by the area to see

entities.name: Heartwood Rewilding Bark Containers
entities.description:
Bark Craft workshops, explore the use of sustainably harvested natural materials including birch, ash and hazel bark, bramble, spruce roots, and willow to create small containers and baskets.

This is a highly tactile and immersive traditional craft, where participants work closely with natural materials softened in warm water heated over a fire. Using simple hand tools, they will learn to cut, shape, fold, weave, and stitch by hand to form functional and beautiful objects.

Bark craft is an ancient skill that has largely been lost in the UK, but remains more widely practised in Scandinavia and other parts of the world. These workshops offer a rare opportunity to reconnect with this heritage technique, working slowly and intentionally with natural materials to create something both practical and unique.

entities.description:

We begin by creating a grounded, welcoming container — inviting people to arrive, settle, and feel safe in their bodies. I then guide a short Yoga Nidra–inspired practice, helping participants soften and open to receive sound more deeply. From there, we move into an immersive sound bath.

We work with Tibetan and crystal singing bowls, large stationary gongs, handheld gongs (allowing us to move through the space), drums, chimes, and rattles, weaving sound in layers that invite rest, re calibration, and embodied presence.

Participants will be invited to rest on the ground, within the natural capacity of the workshop tent with the possibility to take it outside.

entities.description:
What if every meal could become a moment of connection, gratitude and belonging?

In this interactive session, we’ll explore food as more than fuel - as a living relationship with the land, the seasons and the more-than-human world. Through playful reflection, storytelling, mapping the hidden journeys of our food and a shared food ritual, we’ll discover how everyday acts of eating can become meaningful practices of connection and care.

Expect conversation, sensory experience and simple ritual tools you can bring into daily life. You’ll leave with fresh perspectives on food, community and practical ways to weave more presence, reciprocity and ecological awareness into your meals.

Gabrielle Lobb is a cook, facilitator and activist drawn to the places where food, ritual and the natural world meet. She works with communities to reimagine everyday acts as opportunities for connection, care and transformation, and is currently developing a performance project inspired by Joanna Macy's Council of All Beings. She can often be found cooking nourishing meals and weaving rituals at events and retreats, in kitchens and over open fires.

entities.description:
Join Jas and Sam for an introductory Work That Reconnects workshop: a guided group process of experiential practices designed to strengthen us, connect us, and help us meet difficult times without turning away.

Developed by Joanna Macy, The Work That Reconnects draws on deep ecology, deep time, living systems thinking, and wisdom traditions from around the world. Through talking, listening, reflection, imagination, and shared practice, we’ll move through the four stages of the spiral: rooting into gratitude, honouring our pain, seeing with new and ancient eyes, and going forth.

Rooted in the day’s theme of Stronger Together, this workshop invites us to cultivate compassion, courage, connection, creativity, and hope — not as vague optimism, but as something we practise together.

Previous participants have described the experience as revitalising, grounding, connected, profound, energising, hopeful, grateful, and inspiring.

This is a full-process workshop rather than a drop-in session. Capacity is limited to 25 participants, and doors will close shortly after the start so the group can move through the process together.

Facilitated by Jas (they/them) and Sam (he/him), based in East Sussex, who bring experience in facilitation, event design, music, yoga, farming, carpentry, and community organising.

entities.name: Film screening: Six Inches of Soil + Q&A with the filmmakers and special guests
entities.description:
Six Inches of Soil tells the inspiring story of British farmers, growers, chefs and communities standing up against the industrial food system and transforming the way food is produced — to heal the soil, restore biodiversity, nourish local communities, and build more resilient futures.

Following the journeys of new-generation farmers adopting regenerative and agroecological practices, the film explores the realities of farming within a broken food system while asking urgent questions about climate, food security, land, health, and our relationship to the living world beneath our feet.
At once hopeful, grounded and deeply human, the film weaves together stories of courage, experimentation and reconnection — showing that another way of growing food is not only possible, but already happening.

The screening will be followed by a live Q&A with producer Claire Mackenzie, Eddie Reynolds, and Sumita Hutchison from Conscious Planet. Claire is a producer, environmental organiser, and long-time advocate for regenerative food systems and community action. Eddie works with Conscious Planet’s Save Soil initiative, a global movement supporting regenerative agriculture, soil restoration, and farmer-led ecological transition around the world. Sumita brings cross-sector experience in law, public service, environmental sustainability, and public health, with a focus on the relationship between soil, nature recovery, community wellbeing, and social justice.

Dir: Colin Ramsay
English / 96m

Expect beats, breaks, glitch, bass, amens, skank, swing, wobs, brass and all that other good stuff!

entities.name: C@ In The H@
entities.description:
Hailing from Birmingham UK, C@ In The H@ (pronounced: Cat In The Hat) takes the sound of vintage Swing & Jazz and fuses it with 21st Century beats and bass.  His production style is diverse ranging from House & Breaks to DnB & UKG, but all heavily influenced by that golden age speakeasy charm.  
Having secured tracks on several best-of Electro Swing compilations, reaching top 10 on Beatport, and getting a no.1 on Spotify Editorial, he has become a staple household name in the Electro Swing scene.
His DJ sets are all about letting loose and having a good time.  Expect to hear a diverse mix of House, Breaks, DnB, Hip Hop, UKG and lot's of mashups of classic golden oldies.
He also manages Independent label Ragtime Records alongside Tom ESC (Electric Swing Circus) & Duke Skellington (Vaude Villainz), and is a Director of Bham flagship festival Swingamajig.
Since 2012, his music has secured him gigs all around the country including at festivals such as Boomtown, Shambala, Secret Garden Party & Glastonbury; as well as seeing him playing gigs all across Europe, as well as spots in the Middle East and USA.  As a performer he has been blessed to perform with a number of groups both past and present, including Alternative Dubstep Orchestra, Brotherhood of Filth, Emma Lea, and Jasmine Gardosi's 'Dancing to Music You Hate'.

entities.name: Kenny Ken
entities.description:
Kenny Ken, is a legendary figure in the drum and bass and jungle music scenes. Known for his dynamic DJing style and deep connection to the genre's roots, Kenny Ken has been instrumental in shaping the evolution of jungle and drum and bass since the early 1990s.

Kenny Ken first gained recognition in 1994 after winning the prestigious Jungle Soundclash, an achievement that cemented his place in the burgeoning jungle scene. His vibrant, crowd-pleasing sets, combining an eclectic selection of tracks with seamless mixing, quickly made him a favourite at raves and festivals across the UK and beyond. Regular performances at iconic events such as AWOL (A Way of Life) and World Dance established his reputation as a top-tier DJ.

As a producer, Kenny Ken has delivered a string of influential tracks, collaborating with respected labels like Mix & Blen’ and Soundclash Recordings, the latter of which he founded to support and promote jungle and drum and bass artists. His work exemplifies the raw energy and vibrant rhythms that define the genre, inspiring a new generation of producers. 

Beyond the decks and the studio, Kenny Ken is celebrated for his dedication to nurturing talent and promoting the culture of drum and bass. He has mentored numerous up-and-coming artists and remains an enduring presence on the global electronic music scene.

With decades of experience and an undiminished passion for music, Kenny Ken continues to headline major events and festivals, captivating audiences with his charismatic performances and timeless appeal. His contribution to the drum and bass community has solidified his status as one of the genre’s most respected pioneers.

They’ve appeared at Shambala, Boomtown, Download Festival, Rudolstadt Festival (Germany) and Derry Jazz Festival, and regularly double as the horn section for Electric Swing Circus’ Big Band of Boom.

Rooted in the New Orleans playbook but built for UK festival crowds, their set blends classic brass band repertoire with heavyweight arrangements and explosive improvisation. The result is high-impact, call-and-response driven shows designed to move a crowd - loud, physical and impossible to ignore.

This is not background jazz. It’s organised chaos, delivered with precision.

entities.name: Dream Nails
entities.description:
Dream Nails are asking different questions nowadays. They made their name with energised, empathetic, yet politically conscious punk, bursting onto the scene with their 2020 self-titled debut before signing to Marshall Records for their 2023 follow-up, Doom Loop. Those qualities are still intact, but now their lens has taken on a softer, yet no less astute, focus. They’re becoming inquisitive, they’re searching for optimism, and crucially, they’re recalibrating.

Along with this, Dream Nails are operating as a trio for the first time. Becoming a tighter-knit unit has galvanised them all over again as they searched for new avenues for their creativity. “The world that we live in is so complicated, and the old ways of trying to challenge it or make art about it aren’t working for us anymore, we wanted to regroup and find a new kind of creative and spiritual response to our times.”

Nonetheless, they’re not ignoring the world outside their windows. Instead, they’re searching for and connecting with a sense of inclusive humanity. Their interest in stories of strength and resilience speaks to this, as pertinent to one’s personal life as to activism. After all, you can’t change the world by pouring from an empty cup.

entities.name: Vytol B2B Kjah
entities.description:
Vytol‘s infectious production sound amalgamates the best parts of jungle, jump up and steppers and is fast becoming a favourite with some of the most respected jungle/DnB labels (not to mention dancefloors).

Based in Birmingham, UK, he started playing out back in 1999, at such nights as Flashback, Atomic Jam and Broken Minds, which was to become his second residency. His first was at the Blueprint Bar in Birmingham, which, being opposite the Que Club was always a hive of activity. This is where Vytol would cement a long term musical bond with DJ TNT, who would in turn, help him to get a weekly show on Kool FM Midlands 105.6fm, a massive leap in his musical career!
This Junglist hub is also where Vytol met up with long time friend and production partner Kieran J, now better known as K Jah. The pair have gone on to release such highly acclaimed and globally supported dancefloor gems together such as “Trouble In The Streets”, “Cola Cubes”, “Brainwaves” and “Without You”.

With releases on labels such as Ruffneck Ting, Deep in the Jungle, Advisory and Ghetto Dub,Vytol is still keeping busy in the studio with solo and collab projects.

Catch his sets in Birmingham and beyond and, of course repping at Ruffneck Ting label nights…

For booking enquiries please contact ruffneckting.ukdnb@gmail.com

KJAH 
K Jah is rapidly gaining recognition as one of Birmingham’s leading jungle/dnb producers but he fully acknowledges his 25 year apprenticeship in the rave scene, evolving from tape-pack-listener to raver, DJ, pirate radio DJ (Kool FM Midlands) and then music producer.

Drawing on the Rave/Jungle/Drum & Bass sounds that have shaped his life and music from the late 80’s and throughout the 90’s, it’s this history that helps create the substance and vibes of K Jah’s rolling productions.

Between 2010-2012, a string of well-received releases such as Public Service Junglist (Criminal Records), Inception (Advisory Records) and Fibre Optic (Pure Vibez) established K Jah’s style and won him the attention of ravers and DJs alike.

K Jah furthered his impact on the scene in 2013 with tracks such as Clap For That (Ruffneck Ting ) Hot Town (Hocus Pocus) and Fix Dem (Sub Woofah) enjoying extensive worldwide support and frequent radio play from the likes of Bailey and Ray Keith.

2014 has seen K Jah develop and refine his sound further, taking heavy inspiration from his love of East Coast Hip Hop, Detroit Techno, British Soul, Reggae and US R&B.

Releases such as the Supaclash EP (Ruffneck Ting) have showcased K JAH’s varied and versatile approach to producing drum and bass and have achieved high acclaim (as well as high positions in dnb download/ DJ charts)

K Jah‘s dub laden DJ sets can be heard at prestigious events such as Jungle Jam (Leeds), Ruffneck Ting (London) Jungle Showdown (Birmingham). Forthcoming music projects include more solo releases, further collaboration with Jinx, Vytol, Dazee and Dawn Raid, and remixes for artists such as Cabin Fever, Friendly Fire Band and Daisy and the Dark.

For bookings please contact ruffneckting.ukdnb@gmail.com

entities.name: Nookie & Madcap & FiveAlive - Remembering Mc Conrad
entities.description:
Once again, remembering Mc Conrad, This year 3 of his close friends put together a set celebrating his legendary talents and life. 

NOOKIE 
Undoubtedly one of the leading lights in the Drum & Bass scene, Nookie, aka Cloud Nine/Second Vision/New Balance (along with Blame), is London/Herts DJ/producer/artist/remixer Gavin Cheung.

To his credit is "Give a little love", one of the first underground rave anthems, which came out on absolute 2 records then re-released on Reinforced Records in 1993. "The sound of music", (subsequently sampled and remixed by Dizzee Rascal & House legend Jamie Jones) another early rave anthem from "The return of Nookie EP", also issued by Reinforced records was to catapult him into the limelight, "Snow"/"Jazzmin" on Moving Shadow, one of the first tunes to use a real jazz double bass. He was also running his own label in the early nineties (Daddy Armshouse Records) with his long-time friend Pedro, and had a number of releases to his credit.

His status as a remixer continues to rise, not least due to his interpretation of Goldie's instant classic "Inner city life". Other artists to have received the Nookie remix treatment include Cutty Ranks, Flourgon & Ninjaman, Doc Scott, Omni Trio, Adam F, Ganja Crew, MC Conrad's "Energetic Poetry" and The Pedge's "What's Up Partner?" released on Dread Recordings to name but a few. DJ's who have helped promote his work over the years include Fabio, Grooverider, Goldie, LTJ Bukem, Pete Tong and Ray Keith.

Nookie's influences have always included House & Techno from producers such as Kevin Saunderson, Underground Resistance, Derrick May, Juan Atkins, etc and this has led to Nookie's Binary State project which concentrates more on the Detroit Techno side of his talents.

MADCAP
Madcap (Elliot Payne) began DJing in the early ’90s, inspired by a musical family and his time working at Buzz Records in High Wycombe where he met DJ Pulse.

Early gigs across the UK, including The Sanctuary, Milton Keynes, helped build his reputation, followed by national attention after winning the Movement/Technics DJ Competition at The End in 2002.

A long-standing DJ with residencies in Oxford, London, Aylesbury & Birmingham, Madcap has played across major UK cities and internationally in L.A, San Francisco, Florida, Baltimore, Amsterdam, Switzerland, Austria, Poland, Lithuania, Portugal, Romania, Prague & Estonia. Invited to Fabric’s “Bukem In Session” and has been featured on BBC Radio 1, 1Xtra, 6 Music, Rinse FM, Kool FM, Kiss FM, Mi-Soul Radio and more.

entities.name: Jay Dubz
entities.description:
Originally hailing from Wolverhampton and currently residing in the charming town of Shrewsbury, Jay Dubz consistently shares his distinct sound with like-minded individuals. With two decades of DJing experience, he traces his roots back to the sub-culture of pirate radio. Back in 2003 at the age of 15, he received his first big break on the renowned Midlands-based pirate station Dimension FM.


In 2017, Jay Dubz embarked on his production journey after a casual visit from CPH, resulting in the creation of ‘Shadow of the Past’, a collaborative track released on Scott Allen‘s esteemed Soul Deep Recordings label. Since then he has been prolific in both solo releases and collaborations, gracing labels such as Fokuz, Lunar, Influence, Smooth N Groove and more.


Onward initially emerged in 2018 as a podcast on Internet radio station Different Drumz, curated by Jay Dubz. With a focus on a blend of fresh and classic music, often accompanied by lively discussions, the podcast quickly gained popularity. In 2020, it found a new home on Drum & Bass station Bassdrive, evolving into the Onward Show, airing every second and fourth Friday of the month.


Onward Music was established in 2021 with a straightforward mission: to provide a platform for artists to showcase their exceptional music that might otherwise go unnoticed in the annals of history. In an era of rapid content consumption, quality music can easily be overlooked. However, Onward Music is determined to change that narrative and ensure that deserving artists receive the recognition they deserve.

entities.name: I Am A Menstrualist
entities.description:
“I rise from every menstrual cycle censored for centuries.
I am here to reclaim my birthright. 
I am a Menstrualist.”

A live, immersive experience where research meets rhythm, and personal story becomes collective movement.

Join Kate Shepherd Cohen - founder of Menstrual Cycle Support and a practitioner working within frontline NHS social prescribing - for a powerful performance weaving together spoken word, singing and drumming to explore ‘menstrualism’ as a bold, unifying identity within a growing global movement.

Rooted in Kate’s lived experience of severe cyclical symptoms and frontline work supporting people through menstrual health challenges, this is about breaking stigma - and stepping into something bigger: reclaiming the menstrual cycle as a source of insight, connection, and cultural change.

Whether you’re deep in the menstrual movement or just beginning to question the stories you’ve been told, you’re welcome here. After the performance, the space opens up. Through reflection and creative collaboration, you’ll help shape a shared vision of what menstrualism can look and feel like.

Across the weekend, step into the Red Sea Travel Agency and add your mark. Trace your hand. Write “I am” in your own language. Add your voice to a living artwork - a projection and collage shaped by the festival.

Expect to feel something. Expect to think differently. Leave with a deeper sense of your place within our movement - and what we can create together.
