entities.name: Mistress Mo
entities.description:
Mo Jones, better known to the electronic music world as Mistress Mo, stands as a cornerstone of the UK’s Drum & Bass and rave scene. 

Emerging from the mid-90s underground, she quickly established herself as a formidable force in Birmingham’s nightlife, earning a prestigious residency at the legendary club night S.L.A.G. 

Her high-energy sets and deep selection helped define the sonic landscape of the era, making her one of the most respected female DJs in a rapidly evolving movement.

Over the decades, Mo has maintained a tireless commitment to the culture, most notably as the driving force and long-standing resident of Flashback. As one of Birmingham’s longest-running Old Skool events, Flashback has provided a platform for Mo to showcase her encyclopaedic knowledge of rave history while keeping the energy of the original movement alive for new generations. 

Her influence was officially recognised in 2022 when she was featured in the "On Record" project, a tribute to the artists who have shaped the city’s rich musical heritage. Whether she is digging into the archives for a classic set or pushing the boundaries of contemporary Drum & Bass, Mistress Mo remains an essential figure in the UK’s dance music narrative.

Fusing elements of techno, breaks, acid, and ambient, Zobol crafts deep, emotive soundscapes rooted in themes of psychology, nature & futurism. 

Inspired by the sonic explorations of cult techno pioneers Drexciya, Cybotron, & Kraftwerk as well as a deep interest in jazz, funk, braindance and other expressive forms of music. His sound channels both a forward-thinking spirit and a nostalgic soul.

Over the past decade, Zobol has released more than 100 pieces of music across various labels such as 20/20 Vision Recordings, EON, Noise To Meet You, Wave Function Records, Melodize, Haŵs, Nocta Numerica, We're Going Deep, Gated Recordings, Nebulae & Tiger Weeds carving out a reputation for a unique and instantly recognisable sound whose work has earned the attention of leading figures in the scene, with remixes from renowned UK electro stalwarts Plant43, Carl Finlow & Nullptr further cementing his status within the global electro circuit. 

A regular presence in Bristol’s vibrant underground and across the UK, Zobol’s performances have also reached international audiences in cities such as Berlin, Oslo, Paris, Warsaw & he has played alongside notable artists including DMX Krew, Adam Shelton, Jayson Wynters, MOY, Transparent Sound, Alien Communications & Alex Downey.

He co-runs the Distorted Sensory Perception record label, and also curates the Bristol club night, Depth Perception. Whether tinkering away in the studio, behind the decks or performing as a live act, Chmielewski continues to explore and expand the deeper currents of electronic music.

entities.name: Bona Rays
entities.description:
Part of the Decolonise Fest Takeover...

New-wavers from London Town, Bona Rays means 'beautiful face' in Polari; a language spoken by gay men at a time when homosexuality was against the law in this country. It was used in the gay community, so that others (especially the police) couldn't understand them arranging dates, liaisons, etc.

The origins of Bona Rays dates back to the original 'year zero' punk times of 1977, when singer Chas was one of the first black women to front a punk band. A long-lost single (that was only a demo disc) resurfaced and was subsequently issued by Flashback Records in 2020. A band was put together to perform live and promote the single, but COVID struck. And well, that was that! Post COVID, the new band have released two singles (No Connection & Bad Men), written a brand new set and have played regularly across London.

entities.description:
From the Yiddish דאָיִקייט meaning hereness, Doikayt are a new ensemble of Klezmer musicians, dedicated to the celebration and continuation of Eastern-European Jewish instrumental music.  

Bringing together some of the UK’s leading exponents of the Klezmer tradition, Doikayt take their name from the long history of diasporic Jewish politics and culture: the concept of doikayt states that “wherever we live, that’s our homeland”. 

Through their music, community and activism, Doikayt stand in solidarity with collective liberation and the struggle for peoples everywhere to live in safety and peace.

entities.name: Paranoid London - LIVE
entities.description:
We are incredibly excited to share a very special international collaboration landing in the fields this year. Shambala joined forces with Uzbekistan’s groundbreaking Stihia Festival and EarthSonic (In Place of War’s flagship climate programme) to bring you ‘Two Seas’ – an ambitious project using electronic music to tell the stories of two of the world’s most dramatic environmental transformations. A

With the support of the British Council, this project brings together artists from the UK, Uzbekistan and Finland to create original music using real-world field recordings captured from two climate-threatened landscapes: the melting ice of Finland’s Bothnian Bay and the dried seabed of Uzbekistan’s Aral Sea.

At the absolute heart of this project is the acclaimed UK electronic duo Paranoid London. They journeyed to both Finland and Uzbekistan to record the changing soundscapes of these fragile environments, collaborating with local artists and communities along the way.

Experience ‘Two Seas’ Live at Shambala

This epic project will culminate in this headline live set from Paranoid London. Expect hard-hitting electronic rhythms seamlessly blended with natural field recordings and mind-bending immersive visuals, crafted by none other than Matt Black (Coldcut/Ninja Tune) and Ben Sheppee (The Observatory).

Few acts have had such a profound impact on the evolution of club culture, but Paranoid London is undoubtedly one of them. When they burst onto the scene over a decade ago, their raw, unfiltered sound was so fresh it sparked a wave of imitators. Their live performances, too, revolutionized the scene, inspiring a shift toward more dynamic, immersive experiences. 

From headlining legendary festivals like Glastonbury (SilverHayes, Block9, & Shangri-La), Sonar, Dekmantel, and Movement Detroit, to gracing iconic clubs like Fabric, Panorama Bar, Lux Fragil (Lisbon), and Pacha (Ibiza), Paranoid London has taken their electrifying sound to every corner of the globe. Their reach extends from NYC’s Good Room to LA’s Lights Down Low, and from Amsterdam’s DGTL to San Francisco’s Sunset Campout.  

Following its Shambala premiere, the music will be released via EarthSonic’s record label, accompanied by a documentary capturing the entire journey.

entities.description:
Joseph Tawadros AM is a leading Oud virtuoso, composer and 8-time ARIA award winner. Born in Cairo, his chosen instrument, the Oud, is an Arabic lute, the ancestor of the lute and modern guitar.   

A virtuoso of diversity and sensitivity, Joseph performs in concert halls worldwide and is known for his brilliant technique, deep musicianship, storytelling and joyous style of performance. Joseph’s drive to push musical boundaries has inspired collaborations with diverse performers and a solid repertoire of innovative, original music. He performs live as a soloist, in duo with his brother James on Egyptian percussion, with his jazz quartet or with chamber orchestras and symphony orchestras all over the world. 

His global reach spans prestigious international stages, from opening the World Economic Forum in Davos to performing for 15,000 people with the Orchestre Symphonique de Montréal. Tawadros’ immense contributions have been recognised with the Member of the Order of Australia (AM) and an Honorary Doctorate from UNSW, reflecting a versatile legacy ranging from recordings with legends like Roy Ayers to featured performances on major soundtracks such as House of Cards.

entities.name: La Vespa Cougourdon Ourchestra
entities.description:
Born from a decade-long search for the perfect resonant horn, the Vespa Cougourdon Ourchestra is a singular phenomenon in the contemporary Occitan music scene. The project’s origins trace back to the late 1990s, when a quest for world music textures eventually collided with surrealist art of traditional gourd instruments. This vision was realised in 2006 through a collaboration with luthier Jérôme Désigaud, resulting in an original ensemble of handcrafted cougourdon instruments, percussive string and wind hybrids that bridge ancient folk traditions with the avant-garde. 

The orchestra is deeply rooted in the Carnival spirit, inhabiting a theatrical space between wild carnivalesque ecstasy and folk-hero antics. Adorned in elaborate costumes and makeup, the musicians and dancers breathe life into a world of zany totemic figures. Their sound is a hypnotic, trance-like fusion, weaving global influences into a rhythmic tapestry designed for communal interaction. Far more than a musical performance, the Vespa Cougourdon Ourchestra is an invitation to meet, dance, and celebrate within a reimagined folklore that is, quite literally, unique in the world.

entities.name: Sheherazaad
entities.description:
Sheherazaad is an American performer-composer, whose contemporary folk-pop synthesis joins the new wave of South Asian diasporic soundscapes. 

Brought up second-generation in an immigrant household, Sheherazaad gleans from Western classical and South Asian sonic lineages. Her contemporary voicing, though inherently genre-defiant, may be described as alternative folk or experimental ballad. Sheherazaad’s original lyricism modernises certain existing Hindi-Urdu poetic forms, channelling questions of displacement, mother tongue, imagined homelands, and beyond. 

Sheherazaad’s namesake is the revolutionary figure from the largely Middle Eastern and South Asian epic collection of folktales The One Thousand and One Nights, more commonly spelled Scheherazade. This major character’s storytelling prowess brings an end to the mindless genocide of women.

entities.name: Graham Sweeney
entities.description:
Graham Sweeney is a singer-songwriter hailing from Achill Island, Co. Mayo. Known for his eclectic style, Graham masterfully blends traditional guitar playing with rhythmic vocal melodies and experimental sounds. The dramatic landscape and rich history of Achill Island serve as a constant source of inspiration, deeply influencing his poetic and musical artistry.

Graham is an artist who thrives on pushing the boundaries of musical genres. In 2023, he collaborated with Japanese producer Hiroaki Yokoyama on an unique electronic fusion project. This ambitious undertaking merged field sounds captured on the island with contemporary electronic music, resulting in a sold-out screening and another collaborative project in the pipeline for 2025, in Tokyo.

In recent years, Graham has been heavily involved in The Achill Sound, a collaborative project with producer John Michael Berry. This music and history project features a collection of musicians and storytellers from Achill Island, bringing to life the island’s rich cultural tapestry through traditional music and narrative. Their debut album, Isle of the Eagle, released in August 2023, is a tribute to the island's history and features contributions from celebrated local storytellers John Twin McNamara and the late Francie McNamara, along with a host of native and resident musicians.

The Achill Sound's latest project, "Achill Island, Basking Shark Fishermen", is a musical homage to the island’s historic basking shark fishing industry. Supported by the Arts Council of Ireland, this immersive audio/visual show combines interviews recorded by Graham, original visuals, and traditional Irish music to preserve this unique facet of Achill’s heritage for future generations. The live presentations feature audio-visual elements by John Michael Berry and music performed by Graham (guitar and vocals), Lisa Fukuda (fiddle), and John Butler (uilleann pipes).

entities.name: Wooorms Cast by Wooorm and Linear Martin
entities.description:
A commission for Shambala... The Wooorm Casts are trans dimensional mineral deposits filled with shifting colour and pattern, their surfaces alive with geometric worlds that seem to deepen and transform as the light changes.

Inside each structure, light moves slowly through layers of printed pattern, causing the shapes to ripple, pulse, and reorganise themselves. What looks solid one moment becomes fluid the next — colours folding through space like living geometry.

Walk around them, pause, and watch. The patterns never quite settle, and each change of colour reveals a different hidden structure within.

The Wooorm Cast are objects to encounter rather than simply observe — small portals of colour, rhythm, and quiet optical play nestled within the landscape.

Worm - also operating under his human name Joe Barker - is a UK-based visual artist working across a variety of mediums. Beginning with ink drawings using traditional ruler-and-compass techniques, his work has since expanded to include paint markers, acrylics, classic and modern animation, light-reactive art, and more.

entities.name: Old Hag
entities.description:
Performance art meets experimental pop music, Oldhag immerses you in cinematic songs to make you laugh and cry at the same time.

Old Hag is a multi-instrumentalist producer and artist from Brighton, UK, playing with music, sound, costume, installation, video and adapted communal rituals. Performance art meets experimental pop music, Oldhag (Holy Mother) immerses you in cinematic songs to make you laugh and cry at the same time. Exploring how we alchemise pain and encourage empathy, hope & comradery via droll, live performance with communal offerings of pipe dreams and things left unsaid. entities.name: Becoming Crone: A Workshop on Peri/Menopause
entities.description:
This workshop offers a supportive and creative space to explore the intricate connection between mental well-being and the journey through menopause. Whether you are approaching, experiencing, have moved through or will walk alongside someone during this significant life transition, all are warmly welcome.

Ancient folklore can offer us guidance through the powerful archetype of the Crone, known for their power, wisdom and judgement. We will use oral storytelling to open up conversations and explore this through directed art making.  

Together, we will gently unearth the often under-represented experiences of peri/menopause through the power of shared stories and insightful understanding. This workshop blends informative discussions with hands-on creative exploration.


Jess, is a certified art psychotherapist with experience across the lifespan. Practicing in the Bristol area within local charities and the third sector, Jess provides a trauma-informed and deeply caring space for those seeking support. 

Acknowledging that she has not yet personally journeyed through menopause, Jess has thoughtfully collaborated with individuals who have navigated this experience to offer a unique blend of pre-menopausal curiosity and the invaluable wisdom of post-menopausal voices.

Let's step into the wisdom of our cronehood together.

This is a LGBTIQIA+ inclusive space.

entities.name: Deer Oh Deer… Now What? Rethinking Food, Farming and the Messy Reality of Sustainable Eating
entities.description:
We asked the question and you answered. With venison firmly off the menu for 2026, the decision is made… but the conversation is far from over.

Because when it comes to food, nothing is ever that simple.

From wild deer and rewilding to plant-based diets, soil health, global supply chains and what’s actually growing in British fields - the story of “ethical eating” is full of contradictions. What’s best for animals isn’t always best for ecosystems. What’s good for the planet isn’t always accessible, local, or fair. And what we think we know about food often stops at the supermarket shelf.

So where does that leave us?

Join a panel of farmers, campaigners and thinkers as we dig into the uncomfortable middle ground - where animal ethics, ecology, and real-world food systems collide. Expect big questions, honest perspectives, and a few assumptions challenged along the way.

entities.name: Orchestra Baobab
entities.description:
Founded in 1970 in Dakar, Orchestra Baobab is more than just a band - it is an institution, a cornerstone of African music. Initially a club house band inspired by the Afro-Cuban fever that swept through West Africa, Baobab quickly forged a unique style, blending Mandinka, Wolof, and Serer sounds with Latin rhythms and timeless elegance. 

From their first golden era to their remarkable resurgence in the early 2000s, led by Nick Gold (Buena Vista Social Club), the band has continuously reinvented its legacy, captivating each generation with its hypnotic groove.

In 2026 the band celebrates its 50th anniversary with an international tour and the release of a new album ‘Made In Senegal’. This album and their continuing musical legacy are a love letter to Senegal, to its roots, and its musical future. 

Always balancing tradition and modernity, Baobab’s strings and brass resonate with the rhythms of an entire nation. From Casamance to Fouta, from Dakar to Saint-Louis, their sounds explore the rich facets of Senegalese musical heritage.

Rooted in menstrual cycle awareness and inspired by nature’s rhythms - from the moon to the tides - this session reframes the menstrual cycle as an inner compass for everyday life.

Come as you are: curious, bleeding, sceptical, supporting, or simply listening. No prior knowledge required.

Open to all genders.

entities.name: Lamisi
entities.description:
LAMISI (Ghana) (Real World Records) reinvents one of Ghana’s most celebrated artists and women’s rights activists through an energetic new project blending Northern Ghana’s women’s clapping traditions with the contemporary edge, propulsive percussion and hook-driven production of Wanlov The Kubolor.

With a powerful, soulful voice, Lamisi bridges traditional northern rhythms and modern sounds. Based in Accra, she also leads the Lamisi Fata Foundation, empowering girls in her home region’s deeply patriarchal society. Her latest album celebrates women’s clapping music while championing female empowerment and social change.

“The women of Zebilla have been teaching me the clapping rhythms that are the basis of so much of their music and dance,” says Lamisi. “Wanlov and I decided to create a project that would combine this ancient artform with traditional acoustic instrumentation and the synthesised vocals that have been popular across Ghana for decades.”

Across nine tracks, Lamisi's Let Us Clap reimagines ‘traditional’ music, fusing ancient grooves and clapping patterns with studio electronics and heavily vocoded vocals. Tempos shift, tension builds and releases, and past and future move in dialogue.

“This music is fresh,” says Wanlov the Kubolor, the project’s musical director. “It’s magic music. It is the world that we are coming from.”

entities.description:
Bristol-based producer and vocalist Grove makes militant music for the sensually inclined, rooted in bass vibration and liberation.

Emerging from the city’s rich musical heritage, Grove draws influences from punk, dancehall, dubstep, jungle, and experimental electronics, creating tracks that dance between the playful (MILF MAGNET) and the pyromanic (BIG BOOTS).

Upcoming project ‘HYDRA’ marks their boldest offering yet, taking the Greek myth of Hercules and the Hydra and applying it to the state of contemporary oppression and resistance. BREAK A SWEAT and BABYLON ROTTEN are this artist’s reflection of the times, and a call to tap into our inner strength to fight the many-headed beast.

Known for their raucous live shows and fearless production, Grove is carving out a singular space in the UK underground, championing a DIY ethos and galvanising the masses with urgency, defiance, and raw creative energy.

Having made a significant splash in Bristol and London over the past decade via a fierce reputation behind the decks, Manami now sets her sights on the next. Her forthcoming label and productions exhibit a sonic realignment, inspired by a revelatory introspection that has led to a liberatory opportunity of inner growth.

entities.name: AFLO.
entities.description:
AFLO. the poet (she/they) is a Brighton-based spoken word artist, activist and academic who uses poetry as a vehicle to disrupt the status quo and inspire social change. With a bold voice rooted in lived experience, AFLO. uses poetry as a tool for resistance, healing, and radical honesty. Her performances blend sharp social commentary with deep emotional resonance, exploring themes of race, identity, mental health, and social justice.

AFLO. hosts and curates a regular poetry night at Brighton Dome, STATUS FLO. Outside of performance, AFLO. is dedicated to community work, facilitating workshops and collaborating on creative initiatives that empower others to tell their stories. AFLO. is currently in the final year of her PhD research exploring Black people's experiences of mental distress and intimacy. She also co-founder of a local anti-racist organisation, BARCO (Black Anti-Racism Community Organisation). Her interdisciplinary approach fuses poetry with activism, education, and collective care.

entities.name: Sound Bath
entities.description:
Aya Zebrowska and Soesen met at Shambala Festival, when Soesen wandered into Aya’s tent for a session, quietly omitting the small detail that she, too, was a sound therapist. At the end she laughed, eyes bright: “I do it very differently. It was lovely.” A collaboration sparked.

Together they open spaces of deep rest, repair and remembering. Their work marries therapeutic clarity with musical devotion, allowing the nervous system to land while the soul is given room to move.

Aya is a therapist, hypnotherapist (RTT) and sound healer, rooted in somatic psychology and guided by a living, shamanic pulse. She listens for the moment the body is willing to soften, and meets it there.

Soesen, a graduate of the British Academy for Sound Therapy, carries more than twenty years of relationship with music. Her sound unfurls like a great river - fluid, maternal, wildly kind.

What unfolds is a luminous territory where time loosens, defences fall away, and the old songs inside us begin to breathe again.

entities.name: Contact Improvisation
entities.description:
Contact Improvisation is an improvised dance form based on the physical dialogue between two or more moving bodies. Dancers maintain a moving point of contact - sharing weight, following momentum, and responding spontaneously to each other's movement. Creating an ongoing physical conversation without predetermined steps. 

In this one-hour introduction, Rhiannon and Nick will guide you through some basic contact improvisation techniques, using solo, partner, and group exercises, and will conclude with an open jam where participants can experiment with what they've learned in a free-flowing, unstructured space with music.

No dance experience necessary – just bring your curiosity and willingness to explore. We welcome all bodies, ages, and experience levels. Wear comfortable clothes you can move in.

entities.name: Cut A Shine
entities.description:
Cut A Shine is a collective of musicians, dancers and callers who've been spreading their brand of rip roaring hoedown and barn dance music across the UK for over ten years. Conceived in the squat and warehouse parties of London, the band host square dances and ceilidh dances at venues across the capital, whilst spending the summer months darting from festival to festival raising a dust bowl of dance where ever they go. The line up includes Fiddle, Banjo, Guitar, Mandolin and Double bass – the classic “Bluegrass” line up. The show is augmented with flat foot dancers, eccentric and energetic dance callers, and singers, for an all round hoedown experience. 

“Cut A Shine” is not a noun, rather, it is a verb: to Cut A Shine, and the origin, an old-world expression meaning to dance. Back in an era before the Internet, television or even electricity, the local dance would be the primary way of engaging with the wider world and your local community. One would don one’s Sunday Best and shine up those shoes real good, only to cut the shine through rigorous dancing. And therein lies the mission of this collective of musicians, dancers and callers – to get people to Cut A Shine and dance them old dances…and dance them with each other!

entities.name: Dub Colossus
entities.description:
Dub Colossus was the vision of producer and musician Nick Page, aka Dubulah. From the outset, the project was about collaboration with a wide selection of musicians and musical styles. Trips to Addis Ababa and collaborations with Ethiopian musicians influenced and shaped the enduring sound of Dub Colossus. 

Nick passed away in 2021 leaving an unfinished album. The completion of this album by collaborators is both a celebration and a continuation of Nick’s work.

Nick had a remarkable gift for bringing people together, and this live show celebrates the music, friendship, and love he inspired in each of the collaborators on the new album. The line-up features Dub Colossus stalwarts Ben Somers, Paul Chivers (aka Ramjac), and Toby Mills. Original vocalist Sintayehu ‘Mimi’ Zenebe returns, keeping Nick’s passion for Ethiopian music alive throughout the tracks, now joined by newcomer Holly Holden.

The band invite you to come and join in this celebration of music and togetherness — a journey through myriad influences where Ethio-jazz meets the thrumming basslines of dub.

entities.name: Zimbabwean Songs Workshop
entities.description:
Cecilia is a Zimbabwean singer, songwriter, storyteller, and live performer based in the UK, whose music is deeply rooted in heritage and connection. Cecilia was born in Bulawayo, Zimbabwe, where she began performing traditional dance and singing as a child, earning her the nickname “Magida omncane” or “Little Dancer” for her natural stage presence and joy.

Music is a deep part of Cecilia’s family heritage. With a father who is a jazz saxophonist and a mother whose musical heritage dates back to the 1930s in Zimbabwe, Cecilia was raised in a household filled with rhythm and song. Cecilia went on to tour the world as a backing vocalist and integral part of Oliver Mtukudzi’s Black Spirits during its iconic golden years, recording and performing as part of a legacy that continues to live on globally. In addition to this, she has also emerged as a compelling solo artist.

Since relocating to the UK in 2000, Cecilia has enthralled audiences at festivals, small venues, and community events. Whether leading her dynamic band Bulawayo, working collaboratively as part of the Cecilia Ndhlovu Trio, or running inclusive singing workshops, Cecilia has created uplifting spaces where heritage, storytelling, and collective voice come alive.

Zimbabwe has a long and rich musical history that encompasses songs sung at important community events, traditional mbira music, jit, chimurenga and even modern Zim Dancehall. Cecilia distills all of these into a fun and sometimes emotionally powerful community singing workshop suitable for all levels.

With some songs accompanied by the delicate sounds of the mbira, emotion is never far away. When Cecilia picks up her hosho you know it will be time to blow the roof off... Come and sing ingoma zesintu sakwethu!

entities.name: Steven ‘PolarBear’ Camden
entities.description:
Come join renowned storyteller, author and chef Steven Camden aka Polarbear for a collaborative family story building workshop.

Over 90 minutes we’ll talk, draw and write our way to a brand new story full of whatever our imaginations choose to share. 

Steven Camden (Polarbear) is one of the most respected spoken word artists in the UK.

Internationally performing his work since 2007, Camden has graced stages from Kuala Lumpur to California via Glastonbury and The Royal Shakespeare Company. His work has featured on BBC Radio 1, 3, 4 and 6.

A published author, Steven has written three Young Adult novels for HarperCollins: Tape, It's About Love, and Nobody Real, and three for Macmillan: My Big Mouth, Summer School and Cyborgs and Stand Up, Ferran Burke. He has written two poetry collections Everything All At Once was published in July 2018 and The Last Chronicle published by Bloomsbury in 2022.

As a playwright, Stephen's debut play Back Down, was produced by the Birmingham REP and toured nationally in 2015. He was co-writer and script mentor on the Akram Khan Company's Olivier Award winning production Desh, as well as script writer for LIFT festival's acclaimed production Turfed. His theatre piece Mouth Open, Story Jump Out, received five star reviews and toured internationally. His most recent play, I Knew You, was performed at the Birmingham REP in 2017 and toured nationally.

Steven's first Radio 4 play, Sleeping Dogs, aired in 2013, and he is developing an original television series with Expectation Entertainment.

Age recommendation: 8+ but all ages are welcome

entities.name: Shambala Carnival: 'Lyrical Genius'
entities.description:
The Shambala Carnival is the stuff of legend. Genuinely. The effort our crowd put into their costumes each year is truly mindblowing - and each year, the bar seems to get higher, and higher, and higher. Truly one of the highlights of the festival, with thousands of people parading in their most creative, hilarious, homemade finery.

The theme is chosen by our community each year and put to the vote. The Shambala 2026 carnival theme is....

LYRICAL GENIUS

This one's all about turning lyrics into looks, so take a line and run absolutely wild with it… after last year’s show of pun-based mastery, we know you’ve got it in you.

From chart-toppers to cult classics, power ballads to guilty pleasures, protest songs to pop perfection - all genres, eras and artists, all misheard lyrics, deep cuts and one-hit wonders are fair game. Interpret freely. Create wondrously.

Here’s a few to get your creative cogs a-turning… 

Hop in a big yellow taxi, or on the midnight train, we’re off to never never land! Welcome to the jungle, where all the young dudes and dancing queens laugh in the purple rain. entities.name: BBC Child
entities.description:
Being a child is a brilliant, explosive time, and so much of what happens in our early years goes on to shape who we are. But what do we really know about the life, brain and experiences of a child? And what does it mean to be a parent today? What can the latest science, the long view of history and the children pulling on our sleeves really tell us about how we are raising the next generations? 

Join the team behind BBC Radio 4’s award winning series Child as they share some of the biggest surprises, newest ideas and most helpful tips they’ve come across over two series of diving deep into the world of a child. From the first few hours of holding a baby in your arms to rolling through the emotions of toddlerhood, parenting and being a carer is a huge, exciting and beautiful challenge. But we’re also raising kids in fractured societies, with expensive childcare and so much more pressure on every tiny way we influence our kids. It’s beautiful, but oh my gosh it’s exhausting. They’ve also been exploring the world of emotions and will talk through how the latest science might be turning the world of emotions, as we think we know it, on its head. 

Let presenter India Rakusen, producer Ellie Sans and executive producer Alex Hollands calm you down in a fun and fascinating conversation on the very latest on the world of emotions, the world of a child and on being a parent. Will there be laughs? Sure. Will there be tears? Quite possibly. Will there be soul searching? Absolutely. After all - we’re all only human.

Y embody the joy of contradiction: precise yet messy, playful yet uncompromising, untrained yet virtuosic. In 2025, they stand at the forefront of a new wave of boundary-defying UK acts, and with their new release ‘Skipper’, they keep one foot in the underground, the other stomping loudly on the future.

When disenchantment runs high, when city life isn’t all it’s cracked up to be - when you’re forking out seven quid for a pint, shivering in a queue for a club night you don’t really care about, getting ripped off by landlords over blu tac stains, and squeezing in studio sessions around a relentless 9-5 schedule, there is only one logical response: fun.

Synthesiser sounds, a fresh outlook, and a steady diet of early 2000s pop kicked open a world of melodic possibility for the band, resulting in music that’s upbeat throughout every note, swapping wry social commentary for personal experience and big tunes.
 
The band’s rapturous live performance is a fizzing display of eclecticism all with a focus on melody in its purest form. Home Counties always manage to balance the duality of lyrical frankness and musical buoyancy with gusto. With an eye for the day-to-day, all-too-relatable details of crap modern living, yet – coupled with an ear for hook-filled, grin-inducing melodies – the pay-off is one riddled in joy rather than despair.

Her words from the heart speak of recovery through connection. She performs her songs and poetry in different venues across the UK.

entities.name: Decolonise Fest Takeover
entities.description:
Decolonise Fest is an annual London-based, volunteer-run, non-profit DIY punk festival collectively organised by and for punx of colour. For the first time, the collective comes to Shambala for a curated takeover.

It is a space that allows them to advocate for emerging artists of colour, foster a community of like-minded people, connect punx of colour to global struggles against the legacy of colonialism, and indulge in a love of punk together.

Celebrating the many punx of colour creating right now, Decolonise Fest acknowledges the legacy of their elders and the doors they opened, and makes room for more DIY punx of colour to take centre stage and make some noise.

Decolonise Fest centres the experiences of punx of colour, who they define as people who are descended (through one or both parents) from the original inhabitants of Africa, Caribbean, Asia, Middle East, Latin America, Australasia, North America, and the islands of the Atlantic, Pacific and Indian Ocean, and of Romany Gypsy or Traveller heritage.

entities.name: Queerky ft Field Case, Jasseeka Del & Ceegal
entities.description:
Queerky is a community centred techno party, focused on enabling connection and exploration within a safer space. 

Field Case:
Field Case are Bristol-based DJs, producers, and residents of RTN and Queerky. The duo carve out space at the intersection of rhythm and texture, crafting dynamic atmospheres built for exploration and freedom of expression. Their sets move fluidly between broken techno, glitchy bass and hypnotic rhythms, a sound that is both restless and deeply immersive.

Jasseeka Del & CEEGAL:
CEEGAL’s sound fuses tribal, ethereal and spectral elements, crafting a dynamic journey of psychedelic grooves and infectious rhythms. You can expect genre-blending polyrhythmic soundscape, featuring futuristic edges, trippy textures and broken basslines. Jasseeka Del has been a resident DJ and core organiser of QUEERKY since 2021. With over 17 years experience originally started playing DnB on Vinyl in her old life. She now has found a home in the realm of Techno, Breaks, House and Hard Groove all with a relentless minimal drive, full of pounding rhythm, psychedelic twists and acid edges. French-born, Bristol based. 

Since the lifting of lockdown in 2021, the Bristol-based Queerky collective has contributed to the growth of local queer nightlife culture with the support of our home venue, the Loco Klub. 

Their diverse collective consists of 12 members and resident DJs. Through a number of tried processes, they actively aim to create a safer space for everyone to feel comfortable in their skin, accepted and enabled to explore their gender and sexual identity in a protected environment. 

While the queer community is at the heart of the project, allies who respect the ethics of the party are welcomed and valued. The collective is proudly anti-patriarchal, anti-racist, anti-homophobic, and anti-transphobic.

Percussion-centred global music traveller Somatic returns to Shambala with a vibrant selection of left-field techno, breaks, house and dembow.

Raised on festivals from six months old and hauling sound systems into venues by 15, he’s been woven into late-night dance culture for as long as he can remember.

Originally trained as a percussionist, Somatic moves with instinctive rhythm and deep, rolling basslines. His sets are joyful hybrids - 808s tangled with Middle Eastern percussion, electro dissolving into Classical Indian raag - an effortless merging of sounds from everywhere, with no genre borders in sight.

His musical wanderings have taken him to Glastonbury, Boomtown and dancefloors across Bangalore and Mumbai. Away from the decks he works as one of Mr Scruff’s sound engineers, is part of the Daytimers collective, and hosts a monthly Subtle Radio show. He’s also co-creator (with his mum!) of the much-loved, sell-out Dance Against Racism events in Exeter.

Blending atmospheric night time soundscapes, astral synth work, multi-fidelity recordings and dreamy guitars – Night Tapes is a South-East London project making envelope-pushing, escapist dream pop. 

Night Tapes’ debut album portals//polarities is a deeply immersive, genre-blurring journey shaped by place and emotion. entities.name: Grace Petrie
entities.description:
More than a decade after first emerging, protest singer, LGBTQ+ activist, comedy audience favourite and folk star Grace Petrie stands out as one the most important songwriters working in the UK today.

Exploding onto the folk scene in 2010 Petrie quickly attracted attention with her polemical folk anthems, acerbic lyricism and open-hearted performance style. Support slots for the likes of musical legends Billy Bragg and Emmy The Great and subversive comedians like Robin Ince and Josie Long, meant Petrie became just as celebrated in comedy as in music, honing a stage presence characterised by wit and warmth that sits beautifully in both worlds.  

Her career has seen her responding to the evermore dramatic political landscape with her songs serving as cathartic protest anthems, fierce commentaries on unfurling chaos and optimistic calls to fight for a better tomorrow. Her song ‘Black Tie’, a tender reflection on growing up queer, has deservedly become an anthem for queer audiences of all ages. We’re sure to be in for a whirlwind treat of comedic genius and honest reflections on humanity and possibly emerge with equal levels of righteous outrage and hopefulness.

Hollie Cook combines her unique vocal talent with charming charisma to craft her own dynamic strand of lovers rock with enduring tropical pop tones, weaving a path from her West London roots to an arena of diverse collaborations, critically acclaimed records and iconic live performances. 

Cook’s musical identity has been shaped by the reggae and soundsystem culture of 2000s London, the sweetness of Motown, and the emotional intensity of pop icons like Björk and Mariah Carey, all the way through to the lovers rock of Janet Kay and the rocksteady of Phyllis Dillon.

Hollie Cook has transformed her inspirations into a sound that is unmistakably her own, carving out a career defined by warmth, melody, and emotional resonance. Her music moves effortlessly between magic and melancholy, the heart-lifting and heart-breaking. With her 2025 album, Shy Girl, Cook is going back to her roots – tight grooves, beautiful vocals and catchy melodies - more self-assured and more open to vulnerability than ever before. She continues to affirm her place as one of contemporary reggae’s most distinctive voices.

After years of patiently waiting, the stars have aligned for Goat to make their Shambala debut in what will be their ONLY UK PERFORMANCE of 2026!

Emerging from the remote northern locality of Korpilombolo in Sweden, the mysterious band claim to be a multi-generational project born from the region’s collisions of Sami traditions, Scandinavian folklore, and far-flung musical influences gathered over the last century. On stage, masked and costumed, the collective transform performance into a trance-like ceremony of rhythm and repetition. Their music follows a kaleidoscopic vision part ritual, part celebration blending afrobeat rhythms, Anatolian funk, heavy doses of acidic grooves, hypnotic incantations, and serpentine guitar lines.

The band asserts that their sound seeks a universal spirituality. “Goat is mainly a symbol of sacrifice. To sacrifice the individual for the collective good. To become one with the rest of humanity and universe,” said one unnamed Goat co-conspirator in a rare piece of correspondence with the outside world. 

We’re ready to come together as one to celebrate the universal similarities between us as we move to the hallucinatory sounds of Goat..

entities.name: BCUC
entities.description:
From humble beginnings, rehearsing in a shipping container a stone’s throw from the church where Desmond Tutu organised the escape of the most wanted anti-Apartheid activists of Soweto, BCUC have grown into one of the most celebrated bands, delivering electric performances across international stages. 

Like their elders, Bantu Continua Uhuru Consciousness see their music as a hedonistic trance, but also as a weapon of political and spiritual liberation. 

The seven-piece band mesmerises with indigenous funk and high-energy performances with driving drum rhythms, relentless bass and hypnotising vocals. 

Artistic heirs to Philip “Malombo” Tabane and Batsumi, BCUC give a contemporary voice to the ancestral traditions of indigenous peoples. 1970s and ‘80s production and Jazz sounds are fused with hip-hop influences and punk-rock energy, taking the listener on an epic journey, sharing their powerful and inspiring views on modern Africa. 

They tackle the harsh realities of the voiceless, especially the plight of the uneducated workers at the bottom of the social food chain. BCUC taps into the elusiveness of the spirit world of ancestors by which they are inspired. The Africa portrayed by BCUC is not poor, but rich in tradition, rituals and beliefs.

London two-piece Bob Vylan are unique. One vocalist (Bobby) and one drummer (Bobbie). One being a vital and focal mouthpiece, the other a rhythm maker and keeper, one audience ringleader, one master of the calm. They are a band that embraces both chaos and peace, a band that thrives on independence and creating their own path, a band known for mosh pits and pit hugs. They have a unique and ever evolving sound, one that crosses styles and genres, doing away with the traditional and embracing new and more unique sonic dimensions. They incorporate these styles within their music in an attempt to bridge and blend genres and subcultures together. It is this very unique style and sound that has found them embraced by rock, rap, punk, dance and alternative crowds alike.

This band is all about community, and for them, their live show is a place where they can truly express that. With each show starting with mediation, and ending with a group hug. But what’s between the meditative start and embracing end is a message delivered in a way that both Bobby and Bobbie feel has been missing.

entities.name: Emma-Jean Thackray
entities.description:
Multi-dimensional multi-instrumentalist and producer Emma-Jean Thackray broke into the London scene in the mid-2010s when a wave of instrumentalists were emerging. Emma-Jean’s sound, though, always incorporated the widest range of music, from spiritual jazz and funk to Detroit house and techno, northern Bassline and ultra-catchy rock and pop music.

A boundary-breaker in every direction, she moves easily between worlds: firing up global dancefloors as a DJ, directing the London Symphony Orchestra, and appearing at Glastonbury five times in a single year.

Her music has increasingly moved towards embracing her uniqueness and own personal stories with her most recent album, Weirdo, combining virtuosic musicality, self-expression with humour in a triumphant exploration of deep grief, neurodiversity, recovery and gratitude. The album spans grunge, pop, soul and jazz, channelling George Clinton and Kurt Cobain in the award-winning artist’s powerfully idiosyncratic style. 

Thackray played and recorded every instrument, wrote, sung, and arranged all of the songs, and produced, and mixed the whole album, alone in her south London flat. 

Emma-Jean brings humour, warmth, and vulnerability to the stage, inviting audiences into a shared emotional space, celebrating strangeness and resilience through a joyful collision of sound.

The enduring energy and rhythm of The Selecter prove that 2-Tone is still as relevant and important as it was 40 years ago. 

A heady mix of ska and punk born out of Coventry in the 70s and 80s, 2-Tone symbolises the blending of Jamaican and British culture. Led by their iconic Queen of Ska, Pauline Black, one of very few women in the 2-Tone scene, The Selecter celebrated the 45th anniversary of their debut album Too Much Pressure in 2025. 

The anarchic passion that fuelled Selecter gigs during the original 2-Tone era is still there as they continue to perform at festivals and venues around the world. 

From new original tracks to hits including “Three Minute Hero,” “Missing Words,” “Too Much Pressure” and “On My Radio”, The Selecter are masters in urgent, politically engaged and purely uplifting ska-fuelled songs that will have you skanking away.

entities.name: Joshua Idehen
entities.description:
Lately, it feels like the world is one endless bad news cycle. Joshua Idehen isn’t here to pretend otherwise but instead brings humour, warmth and razor-sharp wit to topics that need talking about. 

British-born Nigerian, Idehen began his journey through London’s poetry and jazz circuits honing his spoken word craft at open mic nights and collaborations with L.V., Sons of Kemet, and The Comet Is Coming. 

In his own words, there came a time when Idehen decided he ‘didn't just want to make sad music anymore’. He wanted to pair truthful words with uplifting beats that would serve as the ‘light at the end, something to hold onto’. In came creative partner and musician Ludvig Parment, also known as producer Saturday, Monday. Together they create music that is truly arresting – but simultaneously, thanks to Parment’s soundscapes, often makes you want to wave your arms in the air and dance. If you haven’t heard the track Mum Does The Washing you should absolutely go and listen right now. 

Their debut album, I Know You’re Hurting, Everyone Is Hurting, Everyone Is Trying, You Have Got To Try finds Joshua Idehen’s pen reaching new levels. In these bleak times that try to push us all further apart, it’s a beautiful, powerful manifesto for hope and collectivism. As Joshua puts it: “There's a likelihood that we might be planting seeds that we won't get to see harvested…but the planting is good. The planting is just as important as the watering and the tending and the harvesting. We all have to play a part so that we can have some redemption.”

We can’t wait for what is sure to be a monumental performance from one of the most important voices in contemporary Britain.

Penguin Cafe was founded in 2009 by Arthur Jeffes, bringing together a talented and disparate group of musicians with the dream of continuing and serving as an homage to the musical legacy of world-renowned Penguin Cafe Orchestra, led by his late father Simon Jeffes.

entities.name: Oasis Blues: What is the sound of the Sahara?
entities.description:
Daraa Tribes became a Shambala sensation last year and they're back to tell us more about their sound and journey. 

The band shares the story of how they came together, how their journey has developed, and highlights along the way. Originating from the oasis city of Tagounite in Morocco’s Daraa River Valley, each member comes from a different tribe, bringing distinct musical traditions together. They create a style found only in the oases of the North African Sahara - a mix of traditional tribal music and Sahara blues that combines Gnawa rhythms, Saharaui, Amazigh, Regada, and Ikaaba. Fusing these heritage styles with a touch of blues and rock, their eclectic sound relies on percussion and vocals sung in Darija, Hassani, and Tamazight to reflect a truly multilingual and multi-ethnic expression.

Delve deep into the stories behind this confluence of rhythms and cultures with ethnomusicologist and music events producer Georgie Pope.

- Oud Instruction: Introducing the oud's technique, exploring its role in both traditional and contemporary music.
- Musical Style: Workshops often focus on integrating Arabic maqam (musical modes and quarter tones) with jazz, classical, and world music influences.

- Genre Fluidity: focus on bringing the oud into modern contexts, blending traditional Arabic music with jazz and classical styles.

Open to musicians (and non-musicians) interested in Middle Eastern music, maqam, and world music improvisation.

Joseph will take questions from the audience too.

In these intimate, earth-grounded workshops, discover the revolutionary power of neurogenic tremors – your body’s natural mechanism to discharge deep-seated tension, just like animals shake off danger in the wild.

No talking, no backstory needed. entitySessions.description:
Journey to Iran with Vilk Collective
In this workshop Vilk Collective, Iranian/UK musicians and activists explore the historic relationship between Iran and Britain and invite you to ask any questions you have about Iran.

Winston Churchill called Iran's oil "a prize from fairyland beyond our wildest dreams." From the Anglo-Persian Oil Company (later renamed BP) to the CIA/MI6 coup that overthrew Iran's first democratically elected leader Mossadegh in 1953, British hands are all over Iranian history. Iran was part of Britain's ‘informal Empire’  and most of us were never taught any of it. How is that history playing out in what we are seeing today and what can we do to support the people of Iran? We will end the session together in music, with a collective learning and singing an Iranian song.

Vilk Collective is the boundary-blurring musical collaboration of Roxana Vilk and Peter Vilk,  musicians, filmmakers and community artists whose work is rooted in migration, memory and collective voice. With heritage spanning Iran, the former Czechoslovakia and the UK, their music weaves Persian folk, jazz, dub, funk and global rhythms into something both ancient and future-facing. Recently artists-in-residence at Trinity Community Arts Centre in Bristol, they created the award-winning Lullabies project, (featured on BBC News) celebrating the 96 languages spoken across the city, and went on to tour their immersive gig show Circle/دایره in collaboration with light installation artists Squidsoup, selling out venues including Bristol Beacon, Arnolfini and Freedom Festival Hull and Migration Matters Festival Sheffield. 

BBC Radio 6 favourites and UK Jazz Expo alumni, Vilk Collective’s work is driven by deep community collaboration from refugee choirs to primary schools, creating powerful spaces where diverse stories are sung, shared and celebrated. They are core members of Dovetail Orchestra Bristol, the first Orchestra of Sanctuary for Refugee and Asylum Seeker musicians in the UK and currently co-composing the music for The Paper Cinema’s new production. Vilk Collective have also been commissioned to make documentary films for MTV, Amnesty International, Al Jazeera English and BBC focusing on human rights, cultural identity and freedom of expression.

Brainchild of Lalah-Simone Springer, AFLO. the poet and Naomi Wood, this show blends confessional poetry and performance into a world of glorious imperfection. If you’ve ever felt too sensitive, strange, loud, too much or not enough, this show is made for you.

Travel through space and time with the Vespa Cougourdon Ourchestra, a truly original outfit emerging from the place where carnival meets surrealist theatre. 

Using handcrafted cougourdon instruments - made from dried-out gourds - and percussive string/wind hybrids, this avant-garde ensemble weaves hypnotic, trance-like fusion into a rhythmic tapestry for all. 

More than a musical performance, it’s an invitation to meet, dance and celebrate reimagined folklore. You’ll never look at courgettes in the same way again.

Inda Flo is a DJ, radio host, and event promoter usually playing in her stomping grounds of Techno, Global Bass, Percussive Club, Electronic, and World.


Her sets guarantee a nonstop high and bouncy energy that reach across waters and beyond borders of Asia, Africa, Latin America, The Middle East, The Caribbean, Europe, and the diasporic world. Expect to move and sweat to heavy basslines, relentless rhythms, and certified bangers - accompanied with her signature sound of euphoric instrumentals ranging from brass, percussion, strings, wind, and vocal melodies. This one will be completely different to the Rebel Soul set!


Beyond the decks and behind the scenes, inda Flo is an experienced activist supporting other artist-activists to make creative strategic change in the name of solidarity, liberation, and justice.

An hour of bashment, bouyon & beyond. Bruk out to the finest dancehall and caribbean anthems. Come with your whining partner, bring your bestie and leave your man in the tent, for a one off under 180bpm set from Nymfro to nice up your Saturday night

MC's Jackson Schweir, Kevin Davidson & Robin Clyfan

“What do you say we do what the man says and make today our masterpiece” Ted Lasso

E-Roy is a boundary-crossing DJ bringing high-energy, multicultural sounds wherever he plays. Touching down at Shambala Festival 2026, he’s lining up a vibrant mix of soca, dubstep, UKG, reggae and UK funky — all blended with smooth transitions and proper dancefloor pressure.
His sets are rooted in rhythm, movement and connection. Expect sun-soaked grooves sitting next to weighty basslines, classic cuts weaving into new-school energy. Nothing feels forced — Drawing on sounds from across the globe, he builds the vibe in real time, letting different rhythms and cultures meet on the dancefloor.
Cool and steady behind the decks, E-Roy keeps things flowing while the energy builds naturally. It’s global, it’s bass-driven, and it’s built to make people move.

In 1998 he got involved with promoting electro events in London and soon after started writing music as Plant43. His first vinyl release came in 2006 on the much-missed Ai Records. Several 12’s and the well-received “Burning Decay” album in 2010 alongside other releases on Semantica Records, AC Records (acidlab.de), Bleep43 Recordings and Cultivated Electronics have highlighted his singular and ambiguous style of sinewy electro that draws deep from the influence of Drexciya. Emile is also graphic designer and co-founder of bleep43.com, which is dedicated to promoting and reviewing electronic music. Since 2003, the London based Bleep43 parties have seen him play live alongside such acts as ERP, DJ Stingray, Surgeon, $tinkworx, Microthol, Urban Tribe and many more.
Dj Set - Electro

Village Circus has revamped this childhood classic for adults who still know how to have fun. Expect spontaneous dance offs, surprise bonus rounds and surrealist narratives as we battle to find the most victorious bench bottom.

Part of the Dance Against Racism Takeover.

Percussion-centred global music traveller Somatic returns to Shambala with a vibrant selection of left-field techno, breaks, house and dembow.

Raised on festivals from six months old and hauling sound systems into venues by 15, he’s been woven into late-night dance culture for as long as he can remember.

Originally trained as a percussionist, Somatic moves with instinctive rhythm and deep, rolling basslines. His sets are joyful hybrids - 808s tangled with Middle Eastern percussion, electro dissolving into Classical Indian raag - an effortless merging of sounds from everywhere, with no genre borders in sight.

His musical wanderings have taken him to Glastonbury, Boomtown and dancefloors across Bangalore and Mumbai. Away from the decks he works as one of Mr Scruff’s sound engineers, is part of the Daytimers collective, and hosts a monthly Subtle Radio show. He’s also co-creator (with his mum!) of the much-loved, sell-out Dance Against Racism events in Exeter.

Fraser is a dedicated 17-year-old vinyl DJ and selector from South London. With an eclectic and ever-expanding record collection, he plays unique sounds from all over the world,
crafting unexpected groovy sets that will leave you wanting more. A keen specialist in East African music, (a style he loves for its super positive, danceable energy and its historical and
cultural significance) Fraser draws obscure bangers from the depths of Kenya, Congo, Nigeria, Colombia, Jamaica and more to make you dance your socks off. He aims to bring this
essential, yet often overlooked sound to the beautiful people of Shambala. 
Get ready for a deep dive into often overlooked musical culture that will leave you beaming with joy.

A one-off chance to experience Mark Grists heart and humour in the Family Yurt! He'll be reading his book 'Rhinos don't cry' as well as creating some other surprises. A slightly less sleepy session, ready to move to the common for the closing celebration...

After the heartbreaking news of the Queen of Country's passing, how could we not pay tribute, and bring Sue Wood's beloved Dolly Parton Yoga to the main stage?! 

This very special workshop will take place on the SOLASTA stage at 11am on Saturday morning. It's going to be emotional. It's going to be beautiful. It's going to be pure Dolly.

Let’s imbibe the energy of Dolly Parton and breathe her magical stardust essence right into the heart of our yoga flow to the sounds of her wonderful music in this homage to Dolly.

You’re invited to tap into a little slice of the joy she brought, along with a generous helping of humility and generosity – let’s expect to leave with a renewed twinkle in our eyes and a golden glow to our hearts.

Enjoy a flowing ad lib style sequence – and please wear something that makes you feel fabulous. Let’s get our Dolly yoga groove on!

Shambollox's is a collective of musicians, artists, producers and collaborators with like minded goals and ambitions for the enhancement of Traditional Irish Music Arts & Culture

Formed at the drop of a hat at Shambala festival last year, theres no telling what silliness will be created at this years festival.
The epic Poem of Witches, War and Why the Weather Went Wrong. Poetic story telling, spell binding and spoken word.

Lonán is a queer DJ and music producer who curates sounds that make people stomp and sway with smiles on their faces. He intuitively reads the dance floor to ensure it is successfully stirred up into a sweaty soup. His sets have been described as “saucy”, “smooth” and “intuitive”.

Lonán has played all over the UK, in Berlin and New Zealand, and at events and festivals including Noisily, Come Bye, Heartwood, Secret Garden Party, The Hustle, Camp Crumpet, Riposte and Pinky Promise. 

Lonán plays a range of styles and genres, weaving soulful techno and house seamlessly through global beats and the sounds of disco and gospel. He is even known for playing late-night playful, filthy drum and bass sets when the time is right and has recently begun venturing into ecstatic dance. 

Lonán’s sets are euphoric, and uplifting, encouraging connection and hands-in-the-air joy.

The salty dogs of the Dublin trad scene. If you listen carefully you can hear the sound of the sea speckled in the notes and melodies. But it's not only the shanties and ballads of old that lep forth and soak the ears. It's the modern original songs that stand out and give homage to our fishing and maritime traditions.
Hosted by Jamie Thrasivoulou, Featuring Performances from Nottingham Collective Poets Off The Endz and headlined by Luke Write

From Sibín to Shebeen,

Sibín Beag has always drawn inspiration from the legendary Irish Sibín as well as the vibrant African and Jamaican Shebeen so having Back A Yard come do a take over and turn the space into a Shebeen is such moment for us. 
Back A Yard take over Sibín Beag and carry it somewhere new, from an Irish drinking den to the basement blues dances of Caribbean Britain, where ska, rocksteady and lovers rock found a home when the doors of the mainstream stayed shut.
The Sibín and the Shebeen were both born from the same thing: communities making their own space, their own music, their own welcome, when nowhere else would.

So yeaz better all be on the dance floor

Poor Old Dogs are a cult, rowdy folk-punk and skiffle band from Bristol, UK. Formed by childhood friends, they mix traditional British and Irish folk with punk, ska, calypso, and post-apocalyptic sea shanties to create high-energy, beer-soaked pub shows.

Karyo is a dynamic five-piece alternative hip-hop and ska band based out of Bristol and London. Known for an upbeat mix of post-punk, electro, funk, and brass-infused grooves.

posts.title: A Sonic Bridge Between the UK, Finland and Uzbekistan to confront the climate crisis
posts.body:
We are incredibly excited to share a very special international collaboration landing in the fields this year. We’ve joined forces with Uzbekistan’s groundbreaking Stihia Festival and EarthSonic (In Place of War’s flagship climate programme) to bring you ‘Two Seas’ – an ambitious project using electronic music to tell the stories of two of the world’s most dramatic environmental transformations.
 

With the support of the British Council, this project brings together artists from the UK, Uzbekistan and Finland to create original music using real-world field recordings captured from two climate-threatened landscapes: the melting ice of Finland’s Bothnian Bay and the dried seabed of Uzbekistan’s Aral Sea.
 

The Journey of the Soundscapes

At the absolute heart of this project is the acclaimed UK electronic duo Paranoid London. They journeyed to both Finland and Uzbekistan to record the changing soundscapes of these fragile environments, collaborating with local artists and communities along the way.

  • Chapter One: The Bothnian Bay (Oulu, Finland) The journey began on the frozen coastline of Oulu during the Frozen People Festival. Here, the duo collaborated with Finnish and Indigenous Sámi artists to record the shifting sounds of the Bothnian Bay as rising temperatures continue to reshape and rewrite one of Europe’s northernmost seas, which is gradually losing its frozen identity.
  • Chapter Two: The Aral Sea (Muynak, Uzbekistan) The second chapter took their team and ours to Muynak – once a thriving fishing port and now home to the haunting “cemetery of ships” left behind by the retreating Aral Sea. Paranoid London worked alongside local Uzbek artists to capture the sound of the wind sweeping across the exposed seabed and the hollow resonance of abandoned vessels.

Experience ‘Two Seas’ Live at Shambala

This epic project will culminate in a headline live set from Paranoid London at our very own Data Mine venue at 01:00 (Friday night/Saturday morning. Expect hard-hitting electronic rhythms seamlessly blended with natural field recordings and mind-bending immersive visuals, crafted by none other than Matt Black (Coldcut/Ninja Tune) and Ben Sheppee (The Observatory).
 

We’ll also be welcoming Uzbek artist, WILYAM, to our fields to kick off the weekend with a set at Rebel Soul on Thursday at 21:00 – 22:15 – bringing Central Asian soundscapes straight to our activist hub.

Following its Shambala premiere, the music will be released via EarthSonic’s record label, accompanied by a documentary capturing the entire journey. Lots more on that here!

Big love, 

Sham HQ xx

posts.title: Meet our 2026 Artist: Sophie Bass
posts.body:
Introducing our artist for 2026, the incredible Sophie Bass! The brains behind our gorgeous lineup poster, merch range and lush new illustrations, which you’ll see all over this app!

 

“Hi! I’m Sophie, a London based Illustrator of mixed British and Trinidadian heritage. I make art exploring music, mythology, symbolism and social justice.

I have three main areas of work – in the music world designing record covers, in the publishing world illustrating children’s books and in the artivism world producing political pieces and community projects.

I work by hand, employing traditional techniques with gouache and pen to create contemporary images characterised by strong figures, vivid colours and an energetic style!

I created my Shambala artwork by combining hand drawn illustrations and painted textures in a collage style, I hope it conveys the warmth and electricity of this special festival.”
 

Discover more of Sophie’s work (and shop her prints!) via her instagram.

posts.title: BOOZE, BEER & ‘BOOCHA.
posts.body:
We’ve only gone and raised the bar, again.
 

There’s nothing worse than getting to a festival and discovering your tastebuds are at the mercy of a crappy corporate lager sponsor for the whole weekend. Fear not, thirsty friend, we do things rather differently around these parts.

 

Shambala’s bars stock a whole host of incredible, sustainable and independent tipples, whether you’re a craft beer snob, cocktail connoisseur or skipping the booze entirely, we’ve got you covered.

 

EVRYTHNG SPIRIT

We’ve got a new spirits provider, and they’re absolutely badass. This year, the gin, rum and vodka across all our bars is supplied by Evrythng – a welsh not-for-profit company who give away 100% of their distributable profits to organisations tackling the climate and nature crises. Which means every G&T, rum punch or vodka soda you order at Shambala helps direct more funding towards The Kettering Nature Group (working to improve biodiversity around Kettering), Roots & Shoots (a South London educational & environmental charity) & Avon Needs trees (a charity creating new permanent woodlands along the Bristol-Avon River catchment).

 

May as well make it a double then...!

 

And if that wasn’t enough, they’re working with us on a zero waste, zero recycling, zero landfill model. Every single item of packaging they bring on site is either returned to the distillery for reuse or stored onsite for next year's festival.

 

BAU COCKTAILS

We’ve got a brand-new cocktail supplier and you’re going to lose your lovely little minds over them. They’ll be serving up a delicious range of boozy treats – think Palomas, Bloody Marys, Rum Punch and the most banging frozen Margaritas, to name but a few. Their boozy slushies are dotted around several of our bars, and the full cocktail range is available in the cocktail bar on The Common.

 

Bau Drinks was founded by two brothers, Joe and Ben, whose journey began at their innovative liquid nitrogen bar, Brozen Bar, in Bristol. They’re proper scientists, who distil their own bespoke spirits, liqueurs, bitters and citrus solutions – using fresh ingredients, embracing seasonality and locally sourced ingredients.

 

Their sustainability focus is solid throughout the entire production process – and the cocktails are supplied in reusable containers to minimise carbon footprint and waste.

 

 

FREEDOM BREWERY:

Our main lager suppliers are proper independent beer pioneers, who create clean, crisp pints without compromise, made from 100% British ingredients. They’re Positive Planet certified, Indie Beer and use natural spring water from their own borehole – with a reed bed filtration system cleaning the used brewing water before it’s released back into nature. All their beers are Vegan society certified.

 

Pop into one of our bars for a crisp pint of their Premium Lager, Organic Helles, Horizon IPA and (new for this year) a super summery Freedom Peach Lager.

 

 

WESTONS CIDER

Proper cider from proper cider makers. This lot have been perfecting their craft since 1880, and remain an independent, family-owned business. They source their applies from their own orchards and trusted local growers within 50miles of their mill in Herefordshire.

 

They carefully press and slowly ferment every batch, working in harmony with nature. Their orchards are managed without chemical fertilisers or pesticides, helping to support wildlife and biodiversity.

 

This year, on our main bars you can enjoy a crisp Stowford Press, Scrumpy or their brand new Sweet Apple (lightly sparkling, easy drinking, bloody lush)

 

Cider made with respect for the land, the local community and future generations. Yes please.

 

 

THE WONKY COCK

Our main, on site ‘pub’, the Wonky Cock has a humongous range of craft beers and ciders and cask ales – far too many to list here – from a wide range of wicked small breweries, and all as locally sourced as possible, come in, have a nosy and discover something brilliant.

 

 

ALCOHOL-FREE TREATS

Whether you’re having a sober one, or just pacing yourself…

 

AF beers:

Clear Head, Bristol Beer Factory’s legendary 0.5% ABV Alcohol-free IPA, is available at all our main bars. A portion of sales supports Talk Club, a men’s mental health charity. You can also find Arbor New Horizons 0% at The Wonky Cock.

 

Nania’s Wildbrew

Nania's Wildbrew Kombucha returns to Shambala for a fourth year, pouring proper barrel-fermented kombucha, brewed at their microbrewery in Bristol. Nania's Wildbrew makes kombucha authentically; it's completely RAW, unfiltered, unpasteurised and alive inside. This year, they've brewed a special Hibiscus & Fresh Mint kombucha especially for the festival. Find them on-tap at Next Bar, Talu Bar, and the Wonky Cock Tavern.

 

They source all their tea from the Rare Tea Company in London, who work directly with small tea gardens around the world, championing fair prices and organic growing. Nania's also donate 1% of their sales to the Rare Charity, funding educational scholarships in tea growing communities.  Shambala holds a special place in Nania's story: the brand was actually born here, after founder James attended a kombucha making workshop at the festival in 2019.  He left with his own SCOBY and brewed his first ever batch as soon as he got back to his tent!

 

Mocktails

You don’t need to miss out on the fancy stuff, just because you’re keeping things 0%, Head to the big cocktail bar on The Common for a range of delicious, refreshing mocktails. 

artisanal methods.

 

Karmaceuticals

For a late-night buzz without the booze, find Karmaceutical’s 0% cocktail bar (located just by Reflex). Formulated by herbalists and cocktail enthusiasts, their range of tinctures and cocktails are made with ethically wild-crafted herbs and botanicals sourced as locally as possible from UK independent growers and producers. The ultimate way to fly high, without the hangover,

 

Hedgerow Cordials

Award winning soft drinks made from foraged ingredients. Tantalise your taste buds with the very best of nature’s seasonal bounty. Find them next to Rebel Soul.

posts.title: WIN Tickets to Shambala 2026! 🎟️
posts.body:
Fancy a chance of winning a pair of tickets to Shambala 2026, while fighting for the future of our planet?

This year, our 'Flags For...' fundraising initiative is backing Music Declares Emergency and their Hope Over Fear Campaign.
 

100% of your donation will go straight to establishing regional climate action hubs across the UK - providing resources, training and small grants to help local communities organise gigs, workshops and regeneration projects.
 

Donate now from as little as £5 and you could win a pair of Shambala 2026 tickets worth £590!

 

For every donation received, Shambala will also fly a string of prayer flags from the Solasta Stage at this year's festival, creating a beautiful symbol of our support.

 

ABOUT MUSIC DECLARES EMERGENCY

Music Declares Emergency has been harnessing the power of music to put the climate emergency on the front page of culture for six years. Their small team have created a community of support within music that encompasses all the major UK music organisations and businesses, over 4,000 recording artists and a host of important individuals and change makers within UK music culture. By working across the entire music ecosystem, with a presence at grass roots shows and major festivals they are shifting access to climate activism into the mainstream. 
 

They believe in the power of music to promote the cultural changes needed for a greener, fairer, better future. Find them on site, at Shambala 2026, to find more and join the cause. 
 

YOUR SUPPORT MAKES ALL THE DIFFERENCE
 

The state of the world in 2026 can leave us all feeling helpless, but this is a chance to do something positive. Let’s choose Hope over fear.
 

Dig deep, team - let's show what Shambalans can do! x

posts.title: Shambala 2026 BYOB Rules
posts.body:
A little heads up for first timers - and a reminder to those who joined us last year - that you you can only bring alcohol into the event on your first entry through the gate.

We recommend bringing your tent and alcohol first before making further trips to the car.

This is standard practice at a lot of festivals, and helps prevent people from bringing in huge amounts of alcohol, sometimes with the intention of selling it.

What Can You Bring?

Per adult, you can bring either:

- 16 x 440ml cans of lager/cider/beer, OR

- 18 x 250ml cans of premixed spirits, OR

- A 3-litre box of wine, OR

- Up to 70cl of spirits (not in glass), OR

- Up to 7 litres of cider/lager/beer in plastic bottles or cans.

Excess alcohol will be confiscated and forfeited. Alcohol can only be brought into the festival on your first entry. There is strictly no re-entry to the festival with alcohol.

We understand that people factor BYO into their planning and budgeting, and we’re mindful of that. We want Shamala to be affordable.

BUT...

As a fully independent event, facing ever spiralling production costs, our bars are a vital income stream that needs to be protected. They are also absolutely brilliant - bringing fairly priced, ethically sourced and locally produced tipples to Shambala.

But there's also another important reason, too.

As inequality driven by the concentration of corporate ownership continues to grow, we stand firmly for independence. We have always worked with ethical companies (you cant find a Cola Cola at Shambala, for example), and ours remains one of only a handful of truly independent, corporate sponsorship-free festivals in the UK.

We also do lots of work in the background to research and offer a huge range of ethical, independent and often locally sourced drinks. So, we need you to stand with us, support us as an independent festival, and to create the world we believe in.

Please support our bars (and by doing so, the future of the festival) over big brands and Tesco and the rest.

posts.title: Meet our Rad new Spirits Supplier, Evrythng...
posts.body:
First Plastic. Then Meat. Now Capitalism
 

At Shambala, we’ve always believed festivals can be a force for positive change. 
 

Back in 2013, we ditched single-use plastic from our bars. In 2016, we took meat off the menu. Earlier this year, we became employee-owned. And now? We’re turning our attention to something even bigger: where the money goes.

Because reducing harm is important - but right now, nature needs more than "less damage". It needs repair.

That’s why this year we’re teaming up with Evrythng, a Welsh not-for-profit spirits company who'll be supplying all the gin, rum and vodka across our bars.
 

Here’s the twist: unlike conventional drinks brands, Evrythng gives away 100% of its distributable profits to organisations tackling the climate and nature crises. Which means every G&T, rum punch or vodka soda you order at Shambala helps direct more funding towards people already doing the work.
 

And this is where you come in…
 

You decide where the money goes

This year’s Evrythng profits will be shared between three brilliant organisations - and Shambalans get to decide how the funds are distributed.

Meet the contenders:

  1. Kettering Nature Group

Kettering is 10 miles from Shambala and Kettering Nature Group is a nonprofit community group empowering local people to connect with nature and document wildlife sightings. They run projects including Swift Streets, Bee Barn, and Bats Rock to improve biodiversity prospects around Kettering.

  1. Roots and Shoots

Roots and Shoots is an award-winning independent educational and environmental charity based in Kennington, South London. They run a range of vocational training programmes and environmental projects, with a sustainable venue hire service and community events.

  1. Avon Needs Trees

Named for the river, Avon Needs Trees (ANT) is a registered charity creating new, permanent woodland at a landscape scale throughout the Bristol-Avon River catchment to tackle the climate and nature emergencies.

The final split will be based on the percentage of votes each project receives, so every organisation benefits.

 

Cast your vote HERE! 

 

Voting will close at midnight on Monday 31st of August (just after Shambala) - so you’ve got plenty of time to get involved.
 

This new partnership also goes further than just what’s in your cup. Evrythng operates a closed-loop system, meaning all their packaging is reused again and again rather than being thrown away or recycled.

For us, it’s all part of a bigger picture. Festivals like ours have spent years working out how to shrink their environmental footprints. The next challenge is using our economic footprint to create positive change too.
 

Feeling inspired? Feeling thirsty? Get to know those rad Evrythng dudes a little better here.
 

See you at the bar! x
