posts.title: Wellness and activities now available to book!
posts.body:
From wild saunas and woodland spas to paddleboard yoga on the lake and our legendary on-site roller disco, there’s a whole world of ways to move, unwind and play at Shambala.

 

BUMP Rollerdisco

Time to get disco glam ready, as BUMP Rollerdisco are back at Shambala with their mobile rink for everybody to enjoy! 

Book an ‘unlimited access’ wristband to skate all weekend, or roll up on site and pay per skate. Skates and protection are included!
 

BUMP’s DJs will be spinning all manner of R&B, Afrobeat, House & Bass bangers whilst you get rolling. Open everyday during the festival for everybody over the age of 3, however if you are under 12 and aren’t an experienced skater, then you must be accompanied by an adult on skates.


Remember – rollerskating is at your own risk!

 

SUP Yoga & Sauna

SUP Yoga returns to Shambala for its 11th year – with the brand new addition of ‘SUP n SAUNA’ sessions! 

Whether you’ve never stepped on a paddleboard or are completely new to yoga, there’s no need to worry. Each session is guided at a slow, steady pace, incorporating gentle stretches and simple balance work, making it accessible for everyone.
 

Why not complete the experience by adding a guided sauna session?  Combining heat, cold, and relaxation to fully soak in and sweat out those blissful post-water vibes.

Suitable for people aged 12 and above, if you have any additional needs please talk to one of the instructors to see how they can adjust the session to suit you.

 

The Wandering Wild Spa

Nestled in a wooded glade, you’ll find The Wandering Wild Spa – a sanctuary of relaxation and restoration away from the Festival bustle.

 

Imagine sinking into the rejuvenating warmth of wood-fired hot tubs, the soothing steam of the sauna easing tired muscles, the invigorating cold of the waterfall drench bucket revitalising body and mind – a welcome respite after a long day of festival antics…

Embrace the opportunity to nurture yourself, recharge your energy, and emerge feeling refreshed and invigorated so you can enjoy the magic and adventure of Shambala to the fullest.

Whether you’re looking for an early morning refresh, a moment of rejuvenation before diving back into the festival, some deep relaxation before bed-time, or simply in need of a little extra TLC, The Wild Wandering Spa have got you covered!

posts.title: FIRE SAFETY UPDATES
posts.body:
As you know, it’s been very hot, and very dry, for a very long time. There is rain forecast between now and the show (rain dances most welcome) and whilst it’s a bit soon to trust the long range forecast, it currently looks like things are going to cool off for the show days.


However, on the advice of Northants Fire, our own fire service contractors, and the recent government communications, we have some safety updates: 
 

  • No campfires! Fires are strictly prohibited in both public and crew campsites and as part of venues.
  • No BBQs (disposable or otherwise) or candles (or fire related toys such as poi/juggling etc)
  • On the advice of our fire safety teams, there is no need currently for a ban on gas stoves - but be very mindful when using these, pay close attention and never leave them unattended
  • Smokers, be incredibly vigilant of your cigarette ends - there will be plentiful ash trays around site - use them, do not throw your butts on the floor, and ensure cigarettes are fully extinguished. If you have one of those pouch ashtrays, bring it with you.
  • Fireworks any any communal fires or fire entertainment, will not take place unless conditions significantly change.

Naturally, this is a very dynamic situation, but this is where things stand right now - we’ll ensure we keep you all posted of any amends, so keep an eye on our socials, app and on your inboxes.

 

Big love x

PINK GATE — All Camper Vans, Dragonfly Parking, Accessible Camping Camper Vans and Internal Accessible Parking. Head for Welford, Northamptonshire, take Jct 1 from the A14 and follow signs for Pink Gate.

BLUE GATE — Taxis and Drop-Off / Pick Up. Head toward Kelmarsh and follow signs for Blue Gate.

BLUE GATE — Local Sunday Parking. Head toward Kelmarsh and follow signs for Blue Gate.

BLUE GATE — Cyclists. If you’re making your way to Shambala independently, by bicycle, head toward Kelmarsh and follow signs for Blue Gate.

See you very, very soon! x

posts.title: Safety at Shambala
posts.body:
Safety at a festival means many things – from building the site responsibly, to preventing tent thefts, providing medical care, and creating a space where everyone can truly relax and be themselves.

We strive to provide a space where festival folk from all backgrounds, abilities, ethnicities, ages, sexualities or gender identities feel welcome, safe and free to be their glorious selves. Discrimination, harassment or microaggressions have no place here – respect and celebration are at the heart of who we are.

Keeping everyone safe takes teamwork. Here’s how we do it – and how you can help.

Get Help & Support On Site:

If you require support whilst on site at Shambala, we want everyone to be as aware as possible of how to get help, quickly. We all have a part to play in looking after our community. If something doesn’t feel or look right, or you see someone who may be in need of support, be a buddy not a bystander. Asking if someone is ok goes a long way.

If you have concerns about a person’s welfare, please help them access the festival support services:

  • Check that they have friends with them, and if not, support them to get to the medical centre, welfare or public info tent, or;
  • Ask any steward, security staff, bar staff or venue manager for help – they are able to stay with people who need support, and ask a supervisor to radio for support.
  • There is also a 24 hour hotline phone number published for emergency use and contacting Event Control in the festival App information pages, and the Essential Guide and in the printed programme.

Mental Health, Welfare & Medical:

  • We have a fantastic and highly qualified Medical and Welfare provision at Shambala. It can be found on all of our maps – including in the Essential Guide, Printed Programme and festival app – and is open 24 hours a day. 
  • Our welfare team is ready 24 hours a day with a cup of tea and a calm space to help you with whatever you may need, with qualified Mental Health professionals.
  • Whilst drugs are illegal at Shambala – as they are anywhere else in the country – our welfare and medical team WILL NOT JUDGE YOU for being under the influence of illegal substances and our medical service is confidential. They have specialised skills and experience of supporting those who are having a bad experience – their priority is your safety – please never be afraid to present to the Medical and Welfare tents if you don’t feel right – no matter what you have taken.
  • We are working hard with our medical and welfare provider to recruit more diverse teams, in an effort to remove barriers to accessing services.
  • We have a dedicated safe haven in the main arena, for those who need a break from the sensory overload of the festival – just look for the Sensory Yurt on your map.

Drugs & Harm Reduction:

  • Shambala supports a harm reduction approach.
  • We are part of industry-wide initiatives that share information and intelligence between events on harmful substances in circulation.
  • Our welfare and medical teams include professionals with a wealth of experience in supporting people with substance abuse issues, as well as addiction counsellors. They are on hand to support those who do take drugs and find themselves in need of help.
  • Members of our core staff teams have been on harm reduction training courses run by the The Loop
  • We warn our audience about any safety concerns regarding particular drugs found on site. Please download our Shambala phone app to receive notifications.
  • We share resources ahead of the festival, with both our audience, crew and artists – on the dangers of taking illegal substances – and the harmful and lesser known effects of mixing certain substances, or mixing substances with alcohol.
  • We use our communication channels during the festival to reiterate the process for finding support if you, your friends, or somebody you encounter is not in a good place – due to intoxication, drug use, mental health issues or any other issue.

Sexual Safety:

  • We are proud to be part of an industry-wide initiative promoting sexual safety at festivals – we believe that everyone should feel (and be) safe at all times, and that any form of uninvited advance (physical or verbal) is absolutely unacceptable. 
  • Shambala is already a very strong and conscientious community, with very few reports of such incidents over the years, but we strongly encourage anyone who has experienced or witnessed sexual harassment to report it – we will take all reports seriously and take appropriate action. Don’t be a bystander!
  • We have a dedicated domestic abuse and sexual-assault lead on site with specific expertise and procedures to support victims.
  • We operate the Ask For Angela scheme on all our bars. If someone is making you feel uncomfortable and you need discreet assistance to remove yourself from the situation, ask any of our bar staff for ‘Angela’ – they’ll know what to do and will help you immediately.
  • There are multiple poster campaigns around the festival site, reiterating information about unacceptable behaviour and our zero tolerance approach to anybody spiking anyone’s drinks.
  • We have extended our messaging on this topic pre-event, to increase awareness and safety for woman, girls and non-binary folk (and men).
  • This includes updated advice on spiking based on new national guidelines – awareness, how to report incidents, and the procedures in place to help you should this happen.

Finding Your Friends (…or Making New Ones!)

  • Due to the rural nature of the Shambala site, phone signal can be very poor, once thousands of people have arrived. However, public wifi points can be found at the Public Info point and other locations around the festival – just check the map!
  • Whilst many people do come in groups, a lot of Shambalans also fly solo. Volunteering, eco-travel options and online line social media groups (such as our incredible, fan-run, Unofficial Facebook chat group) can be great ways to meet people in advance.
  • There are literally hundreds of group activities and workshops on site, that will help you connect with your fellow Shambalans – don’t be shy and get stuck in.
  • We have a meeting point for those who have lost their friends to head to, to be reunited. It will be clearly marked on the map.
  • The meeting spot also contains a public noticeboard where you can leave messages for one another – old skool style.
  • The meeting point is located by staff and stewards – so if you are becoming worried that you can’t find your friend/s, there will be friendly faces on hand to report this to.

Lost & Found Kids/Adults:

  • If you lose them, or they lose you, our professional Lost Kids team are on hand 24 hours a day. The Lost Kids Point is located next to the Medical Tent on the map.
  • Report lost kids to any steward or staff member immediately and follow their advice – we have procedures in place.
  • If you are concerned that you have lost an adult and consider them to be vulnerable, please report this to Public Info, who will link you in with our adult welfare providers.

A Space for Grief On Site:

  • Our ‘Love Shrine’ venue is a place for anyone who is missing somebody, or has lost somebody, to take a moment and reflect. 
  • Leave a note, draw a picture or write a postcard, and leave it on the shrine. 
  • As ever, on Sunday night, the messages will be attached to a firework and sent out into the universe.
  • For crew and artists, we also offer other spaces for grief, backstage – however naturally, crew, artists and absolutely anybody are welcome at The Love Shrine also. 

Avoiding Theft & Keeping Your Stuff Safe:

  • We encourage people not to bring unnecessary valuables or cash to the site. 
  • Card payments are accepted at all bars and food traders.
  • Secure lock up services are available onsite to store valuables – the lockers are marked on the festival maps and cost between £3 and £5 dependent on sizes.
  • Comprehensive steward and security deployment including covert teams.

We have worked hard to combat tent thefts at Shambala, promoting our Tent watch initiative:

Top ‘Tent Watch’ tips:

  • Be sensible with your stuff in your campsite/ in tents at night (e.g. don’t leave it by the door!)
  • Know your neighbours – create a community and look out for each other
  • Report ANYTHING suspicious or any thefts immediately to a steward, member of security team or staff at your Campsite Hub (every campsite has one) so we can respond quickly OR ring the onsite 24hr hotline (see printed programme, festival app or the Essential Information guide  for the number).

posts.title: Liftshare to Shambala...
posts.body:
You've got your ticket. You've favourited your must-see acts. The only thing left to figure out is how you're actually getting here... 

For the second year running, we’ve teamed up with Liftshare to help make getting to and from the festival easier, greener, and more fun!

Rather than heading off alone, Liftshare connects you with fellow Shambalans travelling the same way. Share the ride, split the fuel costs, and get into the festival spirit before you’ve even entered the gates. It’s not just a great way to save money – it also helps cut down emissions and reduce traffic around the site, supporting our long-term commitment to sustainability.

So, whether you’ve got empty seats to offer or you’re looking for a lift, Liftshare makes it easy to find your travel crew. Fewer cars on the road, more shared experiences, and a more sociable start to your weekend.

How to find your Shambala travel match:

Step 1: Download the Mobility Ways app 

Sign up with your details and activate your account. 

Step 2: Join the Shambala community

Open the app, tap 'Join a Community' and search for Shambala.

Step 3: Add your journey
Enter your home postcode or pickup location and your planned departure time. The more detail you add here, the better your matches will be. 

Step 4: Browse your matches
Liftshare will show you fellow Shambala goers making compatible journeys from near you. Send them a match!

Step 5: Hit the road together
Agree your pickup point, split the fuel and go. The festival starts the moment you leave.

Fewer cars on the road. Lower emissions. Half the fuel cost. Twice the Company.

Find your match now HERE!

Imagine sinking into the rejuvenating warmth of wood-fired hot tubs, the soothing steam of the sauna easing tired muscles, the invigorating cold of the waterfall drench bucket revitalising body and mind – a welcome respite after a long day of festival antics…

poi.description:

Whether you’ve never stepped on a paddleboard or are completely new to yoga, there’s no need to worry. Each session is guided at a slow, steady pace, incorporating gentle stretches and simple balance work, making it accessible for everyone.

poi.name: Heatwave Sauna
poi.description:
Tucked away in a peaceful corner, this cosy spa is your go-to escape when you need a breather from the buzz. A firm Shambala favourite, it’s the perfect spot to unwind, reset and soak up some serious bliss.
Discover three beautiful yurts - two toasty saunas, and one dreamy steam room. This secluded spot also features refreshing hot and cold showers, and a chill-out area where you can flop, stretch, or chill with fellow spa-goers.

Up front, there’s a counter stocked with all the good stuff: invigorating coffee, warming chai, cold drinks, and freshly baked cakes and pastries. Just outside, the Heatwave fire pit crackles away - the perfect place to gather and glow.

Heatwave Spa embraces body positivity and offers a clothing-optional environment. It’s a beloved haven for festival-goers seeking cleanliness, muscle relief, pre-bedtime relaxation, or detoxification.
No booking needed – just rock up!

poi.description:
The Love Shrine is a gorgeous space where you can come to sit with the memory of someone who can’t be with you - whether through distance, time or loss. We invite you to write a note, a message, or a memory and tie it to a ribbon, letting it drift with your thoughts and love.

As you spend time at the Love Shrine, you’ll be accompanied by the soulful voice of Anna Armitage, who will sing the songs you request, songs that remind you of those you love who can't be there … for whatever reason. The power of music to spark joyful memories is undeniable. The Love Shrine's the place to sit with those memories.

Please send your song requests in advance via Instagram to @love_shrine_ for the Love Shrine Playlist 2026, and we’ll include them in the celebration.

poi.name: The Wait Heart
poi.description:
Fancy a drink at The Wait Heart?

Huddle with the knitters and natterers, share a sip with the old “half a bitter for half the night” boys, muse with the punks and poets, the after-work-still-in-their-shirts crowd, or the families in for one before bedtime. Prop the bar with the muddy rugby players, straight off the pitch, or the hunters in red coats, showing off their spoils. Perhaps you'll feel more at home with the first daters and the drunken break-up-ers, the Hen do’s (and don’ts)? All with heads and hearts to mend in the morning. Everyone loves the local- from the lady of the manor to Mrs Jenkins’ son trying to blag a pint. Their larger-than-life stories will emerge over the weekend, publicly, messily, musically, to the rapturous entertainment of all. 

Do we serve food? Yes, cue the queue for the infamous imaginary carvery! poi.name: Sibín Beag
poi.description:
Experience the fusion of traditional Irish music and cutting-edge sounds at Sibín Beag.

Inspired by the legendary Irish Sibín, and the vibrant African and Jamaican Shebeen, Sibín Beag is a celebration of life, of heritage, of the wild creativity that flows through every festival soul. It’s the laughter in the corner, the chorus around the fire, the cheer of a crowd when the fiddle kicks in. We honour Irish culture - old and new - and the intoxicating energy of the people who keep it alive.

This distinctive venue features soulful, timeless Irish music alongside contemporary sessions that blend traditional sounds with the emerging electronic trad rave scene. Trad Folkin' Rocks will have you slapping your knees and stomping on tables. DJ Annie Craic will make you question everything you thought you knew about Irish dance music and the craic lads will... well, bring all the craic! 

Irish hospitality is legendary for a reason - our doors are open to all. In Sibín Beag, everyone is welcome, everyone has a story, and everyone belongs. When you walk in, it will feel like stepping straight into a bar in Ireland - the warth, the wit, the music, and the unmistakable sense of community that makes you feel right at home, even if you’re miles away.

So bring your fiddle, pull up a chair, and join us for a session why don’t ya?

Ceoíl agus Craíc.

Hundreds of people get them when they’re at festivals. Some of us have been there and it can be a hassle - which is why we’ve developed a dedicated space for people who menstruate and people who don’t but want to learn more: The Red Sea Travel Agency, “A weekend trip away with the monthlies.”

Let us transport you to an oasis of calm for the perfect holiday destination. The Red Sea Travel Agency provides all inclusive package holidays where you will find workshops and talks.

Once inside you’ll find a calm and comfy space with hot water bottles to hand, teas and a “squishy corner”; a dedicated space providing eye masks and ear plugs for those that want some time out; and not least of all the “Hot Flushes” – toilets with sinks to clean your menstrual cup.

But most importantly, this is an education and information hub for everyone! Facts and stats adorn the walls for those who want to find out more about periods…for everything you wanted to know but were too shy to ask.

We’ve voyaged back through the winding streets of fin-de-siècle Europe to return with one of the century’s coziest clubs and bawdiest houses.

Welcome to our new travelling circus home, created especially for you, Shambalans, and hosted by a line-up of outrageous thespians. Expect kids cabaret and family rave-ups, aerial circus swooping overhead, and genre-smashing bands & DJs, all delivered with a distinctly theatrical, unmistakably silly, Compassy twist. See you in the surround!

poi.name: Rebel Soul
poi.description:
Whether on the dance floor or in its workshops, Rebel Soul is a place to feed your fire and reconnect with hope.

During the day, it hosts activists on the frontline, racial justice campaigners, and liberation visionaries. By night, it becomes a musical haven: inclusive-conscious programming, proper punk values, boundary-pushing live music, and DJs playing techno and its derivatives. The dance floor is focused, friendly and fervent.

The venue also features a vegan café and radical bookshop, with all proceeds going directly to the campaigns and activists it hosts.

poi.name: Solasta
poi.description:
Solasta is the beating heart of our musical adventures in utopia, where global grooves meet glorious sunshine energy.

Taking centre stage on The Common, Solasta is where the whole festival community comes together. 

Expect world-class live acts from across the musical map - headliners, rising stars, heritage acts and voices you didn’t know you needed to hear - all delivering vibrant, danceable, unforgettable sets.

In 2026, Solasta also steps forward with renewed intention: world-class sound, bold programming and DJs to keep the momentum rolling between live sets.

This is also the place to head for moments of collective joy - from spontaneous artist collaborations to  poetic interludes and our alway-stirring two-minute silence on Sunday afternoon. 

Welcome, Shambalans, to Solasta - an idyllic land of eternal sunshine!

poi.name: Data Mine
poi.description:
Set deep within a blown-out mine shaft, The Data Mine pulses with cutting-edge electronic music, immersive sound design and a commitment to keeping the energy high until the early hours.

Expect dancing TVs & CCTV watching over the stage, mind-bending visuals, and interactive art installations, all designed to amplify the experience and keep you locked into the rhythm.

A late-night institution at Shambala, The Data Mine is a sweat-soaked sanctuary for lovers of electro, IDM, breaks, jungle drum and bass, and everything in between.

Over the years, it has hosted an electrifying lineup of underground legends and heavyweight selectors, including Storm, Radioactive Man, Frenetic, The Orb, Mantra – all of whom delivered sets that shook the mine shaft to its core.

Plug in, drop out, and surrender to the algorithm.

poi.name: Vivobarefoot
poi.description:
The epic Vivobarefoot are joining us at Shambala this year.

STOP BY AND SWAP YOUR SHOES!

How it works: Drop into their stall, swap your shoes for a pair of Vivobarefoot, and experience the festival with your feet the way nature intended. Wander, dance and explore in barefoot footwear, then enjoy an exclusive festival discount if you decide you want to take them home!

Visit the Vivobarefoot space to discover how your feet influence movement, posture and wellbeing and learn simple ways to build stronger, healthier feet. You can also enter their prize draw, for the chance to win a pair of Vivobarefoot shoes, as well as a whole load of other wicked prizes.

Whether you’re barefoot-curious or already a believer, come and free your feet! xx
